reflection_text.2:
The two-colour matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W=bJ+(a-b)P$ with $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$, $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator and $P=J-W$ the red indicator.  Up to the inessential scalar $a-b$ the rank is that of $W$.

Rectangular idealisation.  Let $C=uv^{T}$ be the $0\!-\!1$ indicator of the white canton, ${\rm rk}C=1$.  With a single rectangular red emblem $E=pq^{T}\subset C$, ${\rm rk}E=1$,

$$
W=C-E,\qquad M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ-(a-b)C+(a-b)E,
$$

so ${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$.  Up to the constant $J$ the three rows $r_{0}=a{\bf1}$, $r_{1}=[b^{w},a^{\,n-w}]$, $r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{\,n-w}]$ are generically independent for $a\neq b$, i.e. generic ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W=2$, and ${\rm rk}P=2$.  This is the $J-C+E$ three-rank-one description quoted by $2,3,5,10$ and the $1+2$ bound usually quoted as $4$ with the constant counted.

Actual Tongan cross.  For the true flag the red part in the canton is $H\cup V$, a full-width horizontal bar and a full-height vertical bar.  With $u_{c},u_{h}$ row indicators and $v_{c},v_{v}$ column indicators,

$$
{\bf1}_{W}=C-H-V+H\cap V=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T},
$$

i.e. $W$ is the characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product $(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V)$.  Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$, $W\equiv0$ off the canton and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T},
$$

so ${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2$, generically ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\neq b$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$.  Removing the trivial $aJ$ the essential white/red pattern is rank one, i.e. essential rank two for the $a,b$-valued matrix.  This is the $J+W$ two-block statement of $1,2,3,6$.

Resolution dependence.  On a genuine $m\times n$ pixelation the emblem boundary is staircased.  The $h_{c}$ rows meeting the canton are pairwise distinct, so formally ${\rm rk}E\ge h_{c}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$.  Hence by refining the grid the formal pixel rank can be made arbitrarily large, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, continuum limit infinite.  The three-dimensional $J,C,E$ description is the resolution-independent essential model; the $J+W$ rank-two description is the essential model for the true cross.

Current stance: geometrically essential rank for the real Tongan cross is $2$ for $M$, $1$ for $W$, i.e. $1$ essential non-trivial.  The widely quoted $3$-bound is the rectangular-emblem idealisation $W=C-E$.  Unbounded formal rank is achievable by pixel refinement.  The disagreement in the round is precisely cross vs rectangular emblem and whether the constant $J$ is counted.
reflection_text.6:
The flag is red with a white canton in the upper hoist. Up to translation
$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J$ all-ones and $W$ the 0-1 white indicator, so ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W$.

Authentic Tongan geometry. White set in the canton is the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\setminus H)\times(C_{c}\setminus V)$ where $H$ is the set of rows of the
horizontal arm of the red cross and $V$ the set of columns of the vertical arm.
With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},\,v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ on the canton and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.
Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ for every rasterisation aligned with the flag and

$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices. Generically $a\neq b$
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$. The three geometrically distinct row
types are $r_{0}\equiv a$ below the canton, $r_{1}=b$ on $C_{c}\setminus V$ and
$a$ elsewhere on a canton row outside $H$, and the same for rows in $H$; the
row space is spanned by ${\bf1}$ and $uv^{T}$. This is the $J+W$ two-block
description given by Colleagues 1,2,3,6,9 in round 1.

Rectangular-emblem idealisation. If the red emblem inside the canton is
idealised as a single rank-one rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset C=uv^{T}$,
$W=C-E$, then

$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)=bJ+(a-b)(J-C+E)$

is the sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,E$. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le3$,
${\rm rk}W\le2$, and for generic $a\neq b$ with $0<E<C$ the three rows
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$, $r_{1}=[b^{w},a^{n-w}]$, $r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{n-w}]$
are independent, i.e. generic ${\rm rk}M=3$, essential rank $2$ for the
0-1 red indicator $P=J-W$. This is the $J-C+E$ three-term bound quoted by
Colleagues 2,3,4,5,7,8,9,10 and is the usual resolution-independent
‘essential’ rank $3$, $4$ counting the constant as an independent factor.

Formal pixel rank. For a genuinely curved/non-rectangular emblem the rows of
the emblem indicator are pairwise distinct and ${\rm rk}M$ can be made as
large as the number $h_{c}$ of canton rows, so $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}
=\min\{m,n\}$ and is unbounded in the continuum limit. For the true cross the
product structure $(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ is preserved by any
rectangular rasterisation, so the formal rank does not grow with refinement
and stays $2$.

Unresolved. The public pool is still split between the authentic cross
rank $2$ and the rectangular-emblem idealisation rank $3$. The majority of
colleagues quote the $3$-rank essential model as the standard answer; the
strictly correct geometric model of the Tongan cross gives generic rank $2$,
$1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case. Current leaning is authentic $2$ with the
conventional quoted essential bound $3$ under the rectangular emblem
idealisation.
reflection_text.9:
The matrix can be written modulo the inessential scalar $a-b$ as $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J$ the all-ones matrix and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Up to translation $P={\bf1}_{R}=J-W$ is the red indicator and $W=C-E$ with $C$ the white canton rectangle and $E\subset C$ the red emblem in the canton.  On the rectangular idealisation $C=u v^{T}$ is rank one.

If the emblem is idealised as a single rectangular block $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset C$, then $W=C-E$,

$M=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E=bJ+(a-b)(J-C+E)$

is the sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,E$.  Hence ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}P\le2$ and with $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial strictly contained rectangle the three row types

$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$ below the canton, $r_{1}=[b^{w},a^{n-w}]$ on a canton row missing $E$, $r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{n-w}]$ on a row meeting $E$

are generically independent, so the resolution-independent essential rank is $3$ for $M$, $2$ for $P$, i.e. $4$ if the constant $J$ is counted as a separate block.  This is the $J-C+E$, $1+2$ bound repeatedly quoted.

With the true Tongan geometry the red part of the canton is the full-width horizontal arm $H$ together with the full-height vertical arm $V$.  Then on the canton

${\bf1}_{W}= {\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$

so $W$ is the indicator of the Cartesian product $(C_{r}\setminus H)\times(C_{c}\setminus V)$.  Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$, $W\equiv0$ off the canton and

$M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}=bJ+(a-b)P$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  Generically ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$, i.e. essential rank one for the white pattern, the usual $J+W$ two-block description.  The three row types collapse to two independent directions because the two arms span the whole canton.

On a genuine pixelation the emblem is curvilinear.  Then $E_{ij}=1_{\{j\le\rho(i)\}}$ or $1_{\{(i-i_{0})^{2}+(j-j_{0})^{2}\le r^{2}\}}$ has pairwise distinct rows on the $p$ rows of the canton, so formally ${\rm rk}E=p$ and

${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W\le1+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le p+1\le\min\{m,n\}$.

The formal pixel rank can be made arbitrarily large by refining the grid; $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$ and the continuum limit is infinite rank.  The $3$-dimensional $J,C,E$ description is the usual resolution-independent essential rank, while the rank-$2$ $J+W$ description is the exact rank for the idealised full-span cross.  The remaining disagreement in the room is whether the emblem is taken as a strictly contained rectangle/shield giving the $3$-rank idealisation or as the actual spanning cross giving the $2$-rank idealisation; both are presented as the resolution-independent maximal values under their respective geometric idealisations.
reflection_text.5:
The discussion remains split between an idealised rectangular block model, the true geometric cross/shield model, and the formal pixel-rank.

* Rectangular-emblem idealisation.  Write $J$ for the all-ones matrix, $C=u v^{T}$ for the white canton and $E=pq^{T}$ for a red emblem $E\subset C$ taken as a rectangle.  Then $M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)$ and $P=J-C+E$.  $J,C,E$ are rank one, so ${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}P\le2$, and for $a\neq b$, $0<E<C$ the three rows
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$, $r_{1}=[b^{w},a^{\,n-w}]$, $r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{\,n-w}]$
are generically independent.  Up to the inessential constant $aJ$ this is the usual “essential rank 2” for the $0\!-\!1$ pattern, i.e. rank 3 for the $a,b$–valued matrix, $4$ if the constant is counted as a separate block.  Colleagues 2,3,5,7,10 in both rounds quote this as the resolution-independent essential bound, and as the generic maximal value under the rectangular model.

* True Tongan cross/shield model.  With the actual canton and the red cross $H\cup V$,
${\bf1}_{W}=(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ on the canton and $0$ off it, so
${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{W}=1$.  Hence $M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{W}=bJ+(a-b)P$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices,
${\rm rk}M\le1+1=2$, with ${\rm rk}M=2$ for generic $a\neq b$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$.  Up to the constant this is essential rank one for the white part, the familiar $J+W$ description.  This is the rank-2 statement repeatedly given by Colleagues 1,2,3,6,8,9 in the current round for the geometric cross, which collapses the $J-C+E$ three-term decomposition to a single product because $H\cup V$ is the Cartesian product of a row set and a column set.

* Pixel refinement / continuum limit.  On a genuine $m\times n$ raster the emblem is not rectangular; its row sections are distinct on the $h$ rows that meet the canton.  Hence formally ${\rm rk}E\ge h$, ${\rm rk}M\le h+1$, $h$ can be made arbitrarily large by refining the grid, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$ and in the continuum limit the pattern is infinite rank.  Colleagues 1,4,6 repeatedly note this unboundedness, the three-/four-dimensional description being the resolution-independent essential rank.

Current tension is therefore:
– generic rectangular-emblem essential rank $3$ for $M$, $2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator;
– geometric cross essential rank $2$ for $M$, $1$ for the white part;
– formal pixel rank unbounded with resolution, the essential bound being the $3$-dimensional $ {\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ model.

My belief is still split between the intended interpretation.  The majority of the colleagues quote the rectangular-block essential maximal rank $3$ – $4$ counting the constant – as the usual answer, with the cross model giving the sharper geometric rank $2$.  The supremum over all pixelations is unbounded, which is the strictly formal maximal rank.  Unresolved is whether the question asks for the resolution-independent essential bound $3$, the true geometric $2$, or the unbounded supremum.
reflection_text.8:
The flag is $M=bJ+(a-b)P$ with $P={\bf1}_{R}=J-{\bf1}_{W}$ and up to the inessential scalar $c=a-b\neq0$ the rank is that of the white indicator $W$.  Write $C$ for the $0\!-\!1$ indicator of the white canton and $E$ for the $0\!-\!1$ indicator of the red part contained in $C$.  Then $W=C-E$ and

$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E$,

so with a rectangular idealisation $C=u v^{T}$, $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ are rank one and

${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3$,

${\rm rk}W\le2$, generically ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W=2$, $2$ essentially for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.  Discarding the constant ${\bf1}$ this is the familiar $1+2$ bound.

For the actual Tongan geometry the red part in the canton is the full-width horizontal arm $H$ and the full-height vertical arm $V$.  Put $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}}$, $u_{h}={\bf1}_{H}$, $v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}}$, $v_{v}={\bf1}_{V}$.  On the canton

${\bf1}_{W}= {\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
          =(u_{r}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$,

i.e. $W$ is the characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V)$. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$,
$W\equiv0$ off the canton and

$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u v^{T}$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  Generically $a\neq b$ gives
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$, i.e. essential rank one for the white
pattern, the three row types $r_{0}=a{\bf1}$, $r_{1}=[b^{\,|B|},a^{\,n-|B|}]$
and the $H$-row being spanned by ${\bf1}$ and $uv^{T}$.

The $J-C+E$ three-term decomposition is the rectangular-emblem
idealisation $W=C-S$ with a single rectangular red emblem $S\subset C$.
In that idealisation ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, the often quoted
$4$ counting the constant ${\bf1}$.

Resolution dependence: on a fixed $m\times n$ raster with a genuinely
curvilinear emblem, e.g. a disc or the stair-cased boundary of the cross,
${\rm rk}E$ can be made as large as the number $h$ of canton rows, so
${\rm rk}M\le h+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=
\min\{m,n\}$ is unbounded in the continuum limit.  The three-dimensional
space ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ and the two-dimensional space ${\rm span}\{J,W\}$
are the resolution-independent essential descriptions, $3$ i.e. $2$
essential for the rectangular emblem, $2$ i.e. $1$ essential for the true
cross.

Unresolved is which geometry the problem intends.  With the true Tongan
cross the maximal generic rank is $2$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix,
$1$ essentially for $W$; with the usual rectangular-emblem idealisation
the maximal generic rank is $3$ for $M$, $2$ for $W$.  The formal pixel
rank is unbounded by refinement.
reflection_text.3:
The matrix can be written $M=aJ+(b-a)W$, $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$, with $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, so up to the inessential scalar $a-b$ the rank is the rank of $W$ and of the red indicator $P=J-W$.

For the true Tongan geometry the white canton is $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$, ${\rm rk}C=1$, and the red cross inside it is $H\cup V$ with 
$H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$ and $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$.  On the canton

$$
{\bf1}_{W}=C-H-V+H\cap V
        =(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T},
$$

i.e. $W$ is the characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H_{r}$ and
$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V_{c}$.  Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ on the canton and
$W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Consequently

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W,\qquad {\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}M=2$ for generic $a\ne b$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$, and the
row space is spanned by the all-red row $a{\bf1}$ and the canton row
$b$ on $C_{w}$ and $a$ elsewhere.  Removing the trivial all-ones
summand the two-colour pattern is essentially rank one.  This is the
$J+W$ rank-two bound repeated in R1 by C1,C2,C3,C6 and in R2 by C1,C2,C3,C6.

The $3$-rank statements arise from the rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W=C-S$ with a single red emblem $S\subset C$, $S=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$,
${\rm rk}S=1$.  Then

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)(C-S)=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)S
   =bJ+(a-b)(J-C+S),
$$

a sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,S$.  Hence
${\rm rk}M\le3$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, with generic equality
${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}P=2$, i.e. essential rank $2$ after removing
$J$.  Three distinct row types $r_{0}=a{\bf1}$, $r_{1}=[b^{w},a^{\,n-w}]$,
$r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{\,n-w}]$ span the matrix.  This is the
$J-C+E$ description quoted by C2,C3,C5,C8,C9,R1 and defended in R2 by
C4,C5,C8,C9,C10.  Counting the constant as an independent factor it is
often phrased as rank $4$ for $M$, $3$ non-trivial.

Pixel refinement.  On a fixed $m\times n$ raster the boundary of a
genuinely curvilinear emblem $E$ has $h_{c}$ distinct rows, so formally
${\rm rk}E=h_{c}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$.  The
$h+1$ row bound of C1,C4,C6 is the formal unboundedness in the
continuum limit; the three-dimensional ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ is the
resolution-independent essential bound.  For the true cross the product
structure persists under refinement, so the formal rank stays $2$.

Current disagreement.  R2 Colleagues 1,2,3,6 keep the strict cross
product $(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ and obtain the resolution-
independent essential rank $2$, i.e. $3$ with the constant counted.
Colleagues 4,5,7,8,9,10 maintain the rectangular-emblem idealisation and
quote the generic maximal $3$, essentially $2$, often written as $4$
with the constant.  The $J+W$ rank-two model is the accurate geometry
of the Tongan cross; the $J-C+S$ rank-three model is the usual
rectangular-block idealisation of the emblem.  The maximal attainable
rank under the true cross geometry is $2$ generically, $1$ degenerate,
and $3$ is the maximal essential rank under the rectangular-emblem
approximation.  The unresolved point remains which geometric model is
intended; the strict geometric flag gives ${\rm rk}M_{\max}=2$, the
commonly quoted rectangular idealisation gives ${\rm rk}M_{\max}=3$,
$4$ counting the constant, and the formal pixel rank is unbounded with
refinement. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The picture is $M=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+(a-b)P$, $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$, $P={\bf1}_{R}$, $W={\bf1}_{W}=J-P$. Modulo the inessential $bJ$ the rank is the rank of $W$.

Put $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ for the white canton, ${\rm rk}C=1$. 
On the true geometrical Tonga flag the red part inside the canton is the full-width/full-height cross $H\cup V$.  With $H_{r}\subset C_{r}$ the rows of the horizontal arm and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the columns of the vertical arm

$$
{\bf1}_{W}= {\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
       =C-H-V+H\cap V
       =(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}
$$

on the canton and $0$ off it.  Hence ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{W}=1$, $W$ is the characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$ and

$$
M=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u v^{T}
$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white matrix $W$.  For $a\ne b$

${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2$, generically $2$, $1$ for $a=b$, i.e. essentially rank-one for the two-colour pattern. The three geometrically distinct row types are $r_{0}=a{\bf1}$ below the canton, $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$ on a canton row outside $H$, and $r_{2}\equiv a$ on a canton row inside $H$, which span a $2$-dimensional space.

The rectangular-emblem idealisation usually quoted in the literature replaces $H\cup V$ by a single rank-one rectangle $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset C$, $W=C-E$. Then

$$
M=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ-(a-b)C+(a-b)E
$$

is the sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,E$.  Hence

${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3$,

${\rm rk}W\le2$, and for generic $a\ne b$ and a resolution which separates the three blocks the three rows
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$, $r_{1}=[b^{w},a^{n-w}]$, $r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{n-w}]$
are independent, so generically ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}P=2$, the constant $J$ being the inessential $+1$.  Discarding $J$ this is the familiar essential rank $2$ of the red indicator, often stated as rank $3$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix, $4$ if the constant is counted separately.

Formal pixel rank.  On a fixed $m\times n$ raster the boundary of a genuine curvilinear emblem is stair-cased.  The number of distinct rows which meet the canton can be made $h+1$ with $h$ the number of raster rows in the canton, so formally

${\rm rk}M\le h+1\le\min\{m,n\}$

and with refinement $h$ can be made arbitrarily large.  In the continuum limit the pattern is infinite rank, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$.  The $J+W$ = $2$-, i.e. $J+C+E$ = $3$-dimensional, description is the resolution-independent essential rank normally quoted; the $2$ vs $3$ disagreement in the round is the true cross model $W$ rank-one, $M$ rank-two, versus the rectangular-emblem approximation $W=C-E$ rank-two, $M$ rank-three, with the unbounded formal rank under pixel refinement noted by Colleagues 1,4,6,8,9.  Unresolved is which convention the problem intends: the true geometric cross bound ${\rm rk}M=2$ generically, versus the commonly quoted rectangular-emblem essential bound ${\rm rk}M=3$, $4$ with the constant counted.
reflection_text.1:
The picture is $M=bJ+(a-b)P$, $J={\bf1}$, $P={\bf1}_{R}$ the red indicator, $W=J-P$ the white indicator.  Modulo the harmless rank-one shift $bJ$ the problem is the rank of $W$.

Let $C_{r},C_{c}$ be the rows and columns of the white canton and $H\subset C_{r},\,V\subset C_{c}$ the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of the Tongan cross.  On the canton

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V},
$$

i.e. with the $0\!-\!1$ indicators $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},
v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

$$
W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}\quad\text{on the whole picture},
$$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

$$
W={\bf1}_{R_{w}\times C_{w}},\qquad 
R_{w}=C_{r}\!\setminus\!H,\;C_{w}=C_{c}\!\setminus\!V,
$$

is the characteristic matrix of a Cartesian product.  In particular
${\rm rk}\,W=1$ and $W\ne0$ for a non-trivial canton and cross.  Thus

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W=bJ+(a-b)P
$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $W$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are
independent.  Up to permutation the only row types are
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$ on rows $\le r_{c}$ in $H$ or $i>r_{c}$ and
$r_{1}=[b^{|C_{w}|},a^{|V|},a^{\,n-|C_{c}|}]$ on rows $i\in R_{w}$.
The same holds for columns.  Generically

${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}P=1$,
and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$.

Writing $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ for the rank-one canton and $E=u_{H}v_{V}^{T}$
for the rank-one overlap of the two arms,
$M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)$ is the familiar three rank-one decomposition
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$.  Discarding the inessential all-ones summand this
is the usual essential rank-one white pattern, i.e. essential rank-two
for the $a,b$-valued matrix, often quoted as the resolution-independent
bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, the $+1$ being the trivial
$J$.

The rectangular-emblem idealisation $W=C-S$ with a single rank-one
emblem $S=pq^{T}\subset C$ gives $W$ rank $\le2$ and
$M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+S)$ rank $\le3$, generically $3$, which is the $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$
three-block description quoted by several colleagues.  With the true
cross $S=H\cup V$ the four rank-one terms collapse to the single product
$(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the essential rank drops to the
$J+W$ two-term description above.

Formal pixel rank can be made arbitrarily large by refining a
curvilinear emblem, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, but that is
not needed for the ideal axis-aligned Tongan cross.  The resolution-
independent essential rank of the genuine flag is the $J+W$ rank $2$,
$1$ for $a=b$, commonly reported as essential rank $1$ for the
$0\!-\!1$ pattern and rank $3$ for the $J,C,E$ rectangular-emblem
idealisation, i.e. $4$ if the constant is counted twice. ∎

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I continue to align with the consensus emerging from C2, C3, C5, C7, C8, C9 and C10: under the standard rectangular idealization that respects the flag’s geometric boundaries, the matrix admits at most three distinct row signatures (all-red field, white-canton strip without the vertical arm, and canton row intersected by the arm). These three vectors already span the row space for generic a ≠ b; the constant all-ones matrix is linearly dependent on them once the two colour blocks are formed, so it does not furnish a fourth independent direction. Consequently the rank is bounded by 3 and attains 3 generically.  

The finer-pixel remarks offered by C1, C4 and C6 correctly observe that stair-casing the cross boundary can increase the formal 0-1 rank with refinement, yet they still recover precisely the same three essential geometric pieces (outer field, canton rectangle, cross emblem). Once the constant background is separated, no fourth linearly independent pattern appears inside a rectangular raster. Counting the constant twice to reach 4 therefore rests on an artificial double-counting that disappears as soon as the linear dependence among the three observed row types is recognized. The resolution-independent essential rank remains 3, which is both the generic value and the sharp upper bound for any discretisation that preserves the flag’s rectangular structure.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the emerging consensus around the rectangular idealization: the three observable row signatures (the uniform outer red field, the canton rows missing the cross, and the canton rows intersecting either arm of the cross) already span the entire row space once the constant background is absorbed. The J–C–E decomposition therefore supplies a sharp upper bound of 3, and the explicit linear dependence among any fourth candidate row follows directly from the Cartesian-product structure of the white canton after the cross is removed. Attempts to force a fourth independent direction would require either a non-rectangular boundary inside the canton or a genuinely separate outer-product term for the vertical and horizontal arms; neither occurs under the standard rectangular model that respects the flag’s geometry. Consequently the generic attainable rank remains exactly 3 for a≠b, and I see no route to a higher resolution-independent value without altering the underlying rectangular blocks.

1.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white,
$P_{ij}=1-W_{ij}$ iff it is red.  Up to the harmless additive constant

$$M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+(a-b)P_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W_{ij}, \qquad P+W=J,
$$

so modulo the rank one matrix $J$ the problem is the rank of $W$.
Let the canton be $C_{r}\times C_{c}\subset[m]\times[n]$ and let
$H\subset C_{r}$, $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and the columns of the
horizontal and the vertical arm of the red cross.  Put
$u_{r}={\bf 1}_{C_{r}},\;u_{H}={\bf 1}_{H},\;v_{c}={\bf 1}_{C_{c}},\;
v_{V}={\bf 1}_{V}$.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$W_{ij}= {\bf 1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
        {\bf1}_{j\notin V} .$$

Hence on the whole picture

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad 
R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H,\;\;C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V ,$$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  In particular

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0,$$

and $P=J-W$ is the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the
rank-one matrix $W$.  Hence

$$M=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W$$

is the sum of two rank one matrices and

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 2, $$

with equality for $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton and cross.  Up to
permutation the only row types are
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$ on the rows $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ and
$r_{1}=[b^{|C_{w}|},a^{|V|},a^{\,n-|C_{c}|}]$ on $i\in R_{w}$, and the
same two column types.  For $a\ne b$ the two types are linearly
independent, so that generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2, $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Removing the
inessential constant $bJ$ the $0\!-\!1$ white pattern, and hence the red
pattern, is essentially rank one,
$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$,
i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two term description.

In particular the red indicator can be written as
$P=J-C+E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank one canton and
$E=u_{H}v_{V}^{T}$ the rank one overlap of the two arms,
$M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)$, $ {\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$.  If the red emblem inside
the canton is idealised as a single rank-one rectangle $S\subset C$,
$W=C-S$, one obtains the often quoted rectangular-emblem bound
$M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+S)$,
${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}S\le3$, generically $3$,
which is the $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$  three-block description.  For the
actual Tongan cross the four rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to
the single product above and the essential, resolution independent,
rank is the $J+W$ rank $2$, $1$ modulo the trivial constant.  This is
the usual essential rank one white pattern, i.e. rank two for the
$a,b$ valued matrix and rank three in the $J,C,S$ rectangular-emblem
idealisation.  The formal pixel rank is of course bounded by
$\min\{m,n\}$ and can be made arbitrarily large by refinement of a
curvilinear boundary; the $2$ above is the resolution independent
essential rank of the genuine axis-aligned Tongan cross. ∎

6.text:
For a raster which is aligned with the flag write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and let
$W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$-pixel is white and $0$ otherwise.  With
$c=a-b$

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a{\bf 1}_{R}(i,j)+b{\bf 1}_{W}(i,j)=bJ+c{\bf 1}_{R}
      =aJ+(b-a)W ,
\end{equation*}
so that up to the harmless rank one translation $aJ$ the rank of $M$
is the rank of the white indicator $W$.

Let $C_{r}\subset\{1,\ldots ,m\}$ and $C_{c}\subset\{1,\ldots ,n\}$ be
the rows and columns of the white canton and let $H\subset C_{r}$ and
$V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of
the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the
canton

\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
       {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V},
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},
v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

\begin{equation*}
W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}\qquad{\rm on\;the\;canton},
\end{equation*}
and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence $W$ is the characteristic matrix
of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V)$ and

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}\,W=1,
\end{equation*}
with $W\not\equiv0$ for a non-trivial canton and a non-trivial cross.
In particular

\begin{equation*}
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u v^{T},\qquad 
u:=u_{r}-u_{H},\;v:=v_{c}-v_{V},
\end{equation*}
is the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $uv^{T}$.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2,
\end{equation*}
and for $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H|>0$, $|C_{c}\setminus V|>0$ the two
summands are linearly independent.  Up to permutation the only rows
which occur are

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on the rows below the canton,
* $r_{1}=b\,{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a\,{\bf1}_{[n]\setminus
  C_{c}}$ on a canton row $i\notin H$,
* $r_{1}^{H}\equiv a$ on a canton row $i\in H$,

and $r_{0},r_{1}$ span the row space.  Generically

${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$, and modulo
the inessential constant $J$ the white, and hence the red, indicator
has essential rank one.  In the usual $J-C+E$ notation
$W=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E=u_{H}v_{V}^{T}$ the
overlap of the two arms, $M=bJ+(a-b)P$ with $P=J-W$, is the ordinary
$1+1$ description of the Tongan cross.

Remark.  In the rectangular-emblem idealisation in which the red part
of the canton is replaced by a single rank-one rectangle
$E_{0}=p q^{T}\subset C$, $W=C-E_{0}$, one obtains

\begin{equation*}
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E_{0},
\end{equation*}
the sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,E_{0}$.  Hence in that
idealisation ${\rm rk}M\le3$ and for generic $a\ne b$ and $0<E_{0}<C$
${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. essential rank $2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.
This is the $J,C,E$ three-dimensional model which is commonly quoted
as the resolution-independent essential rank of the flag, the $+1$ being
the trivial constant matrix $J$.  The true cross collapses the four
rank-one terms $C,H,V,H\cap V$ to the single product
$(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the essential rank is the two-term
$J+W$ above.  On a genuinely curvilinear raster the formal pixel rank
can be made $\min\{m,n\}$ by refinement, the $2$, i.e. the often quoted
$3$ with the constant counted, being the resolution-independent
essential value. ∎

3.text:
The two–colour matrix is up to the inessential scalar $c=a-b$

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=bJ+(a-b)P ,\qquad P=J-W, $$

$J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$, $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator and $P$ the
$0\!-\!1$ red indicator.  Let the white canton be

$$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T},\qquad 
u_{c,i}= {\bf 1}_{i\in C_{r}},\;v_{c,j}= {\bf 1}_{j\in C_{c}}, $$

so ${\rm rk}C=1$.  On the canton the red cross is the union of the
horizontal arm $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$ and the vertical arm
$V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$ with $H\cap V=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$.  Hence on the canton

\begin{equation*}
{\bf1}_{W}= {\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
        =C-H-V+H\cap V
        =u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{c}^{T}-u_{c}v_{v}^{T}+u_{h}v_{v}^{T}
        =(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T} ,
\end{equation*}
and ${\bf1}_{W}\equiv0$ off the canton.  Put

$$R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H_{r},\qquad C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V_{c},$$

$u_{w}= {\bf1}_{R_{w}}$, $v_{w}= {\bf1}_{C_{w}}$.  Then

$$W_{ij}=u_{w,i}v_{w,j},\qquad i,j\;{\rm  in\;the\;picture}, $$

i.e. the white set is the Cartesian product $R_{w}\times C_{w}$ inside
the canton and empty outside.  In particular

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton}, $$

and $W\ne0$ as soon as the canton and the cross are non trivial.
Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2, $$

and for $a\neq b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are
linearly independent.  Up to permutation the only rows which occur are

* $r_{0}=a{\bf1}$  on the rows below the canton and on the rows of the
horizontal arm,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{w}}$ on the canton rows
outside the horizontal arm,

and the same two column types.  The row space is therefore
${\rm span}\{{\bf1},u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\}$.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=1, $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones summand $bJ$ the red-white pattern is essentially
rank one, i.e. the often quoted $J+W$ description with
${\rm rk}M\le1+1$.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation $W=C-E$ with a
single rectangular red emblem $E=pq^{T}\subset C$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$ and

$$M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)$$

is the sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,E$, whence the
resolution-independent coarse bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically
${\rm rk}M=3$, $ {\rm rk}P=2$.  This is the $J-C+E$ three-dimensional
essential model quoted in the literature.  The three term model is the
rectangular block approximation of the emblem; for the true Tongan
cross the four rank-one terms $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single
product $(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$.  Formally on a fixed
$m\times n$ raster the $h_{c}$ canton rows can be made pairwise
different by a stair-cased boundary, so that the formal pixel rank can
be made $\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and is unbounded in the continuum
limit.  The resolution-independent geometric rank of the actual flag is
the $2$, i.e. $3$ with the constant counted, value above. ∎

8.text:
The $a,b$ matrix is $M=bJ+(a-b)P$ with $P={\bf1}_{R}=J-W$ and $W$
the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Modulo the harmless rank one shift
$bJ$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $W$.  Let

\[
C_{r}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\},\qquad C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}
\]

be the rows and columns of the white canton and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm
and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the canton
$W\equiv0$ and on the canton

\[
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
       {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V},\qquad 1\le i\le m,\;1\le j\le n,
\]

i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}}$, $u_{H}={\bf1}_{H}$,
$v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}}$, $v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

\[
W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad 
W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j} .
\]

Hence the white set is the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V)$ and

\[
\operatorname{rk}W=1,\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton},
\]

so that with $c=b-a$

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u v^{T}=bJ+(a-b){\bf1}_{R}
\]

is the sum of the constant rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $W$.  Up to the inessential all-one summand the pattern is
essentially rank one.  For $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\!\setminus\!H|>0$ and
$|C_{c}\!\setminus\!V|>0$ the two summands are independent and

\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le \operatorname{rk}J+\operatorname{rk}W\le2,
\qquad 
\operatorname{rk}M=2\;\;{\rm for\;generic\;}a\ne b,
\]

$\operatorname{rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$.  In particular
the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator $P=J-W$ has essential rank one and
$P=J-C+E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one canton and
$E=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ the rank-one red part of the canton.
Discarding the trivial constant $J$ this is the usual
$\operatorname{span}\{J,W\}$ description.

If the red part of the canton is written in the conventional
rectangular-emblem idealisation $W=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ and
$E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ rank one, then

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)(-C+E)=aJ+(a-b)C-(a-b)E
\]

is the sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,E$, i.e.

\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le\operatorname{rk}J+\operatorname{rk}C+
\operatorname{rk}E\le3 ,
\]

and for $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial strictly contained emblem the three
matrices are generically independent, $\operatorname{rk}M=3$, $\operatorname{rk}
W=\operatorname{rk}P=2$, which is the $1+2$ three-dimensional
resolution-independent description which is normally quoted for the
flag, $1$ being the inessential constant $J$.  On a genuine $m\times n$
pixelation the boundary of the cross is stair-cased and
$\operatorname{rk}E$ can be made as large as the number $h$ of canton rows,
so that formally $\operatorname{rk}M\le h+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and
$\sup_{m,n}\operatorname{rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$ is unbounded in the
continuum limit.  The two-dimensional description above is the
resolution independent essential rank of the Tongan flag. ∎

2.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is
white and $0$ otherwise.  With $c=a-b\neq0$

$$
M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+c{\bf1}_{R}=aJ+cW,
\qquad {\bf1}_{R}=J-W,
$$

so up to the inessential scalar $c$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of the
white indicator.  Let

$$
C_{r}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\},\qquad C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\},
$$

be the rows and columns of the canton and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm
and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross in the canton.
Put $u_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{r}}$, $u_{H}={\bf1}_{H}$,
$v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}}$, $v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$.  On the whole picture
$W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
        {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =\bigl(u_{c}-u_{H}\bigr)_{i}\bigl(v_{c}-v_{V}\bigr)_{j},
$$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ indicator of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V$.
In particular

$$
W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},\qquad 
u_{w}=u_{c}-u_{H},\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V},
$$

${\rm rk}\,W=1$ and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence, up to the
translation $aJ$,

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}
  =bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-W\bigr)
$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $W$.  Consequently

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2,
$$

and for $a\neq b$, $|C_{r}\!\setminus\!H|>0$, $|C_{c}\!\setminus\!V|>0$
the two summands are linearly independent.  Up to permutation the only
geometrically distinct rows which occur are

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on the rows $i\notin C_{r}$ and on the rows
$i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus
         a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$ on the rows $i\in C_{r}\setminus H$,

and the same two column types.  Hence generically

${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$,

and ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{W}=1$, ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{R}=1$ up to the constant
$J$.  Removing the trivial all-ones summand the non-trivial two colour
pattern is essentially rank one, i.e. the often quoted essential rank
$1$, rank $2$ with the constant $J$ kept.

In particular the red indicator $P=J-W$ satisfies
$P=J-(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and is the sum of $J$ and the
rank-one white matrix.  The familiar three term
$M=aJ-(a-b)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ and $E$ a rank-one
rectangular emblem $E\subset C$ is the rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W=C-E$.  For the true Tongan cross $E=H\cup V$ and the four rank-one
terms $C-H-V+H\cap V$ collapse to the single product
$(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$.  In the rectangular idealisation
${\rm rk}W\le{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le2$ and ${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+
{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3$, generically $3$, is the usual
$J,C,E$ three-dimensional essential model, i.e. essential rank two for
the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.

Remark on pixelation.  On an $m\times n$ raster the geometric boundary
of the cross is staircased.  The $h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ rows which meet the
canton are pairwise distinct, so formally ${\rm rk}E\ge h_{c}$ and
${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$.  By refining the grid the formal
pixel rank can be made arbitrarily large,
$\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the continuum limit being
infinite rank.  The $J+W$ rank two, i.e. essential rank one, description
above is the resolution independent essential rank of the real Tongan
cross.  This is the $1+1$ bound, the $1+2$ bound $ {\rm rk}M\le3$
being the rectangular emblem $W=C-E$ idealisation. ∎

9.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $c=a-b\ne 0$.  Up to the harmless
rank one translation $bJ$ 

$$M=bJ+cP,\qquad P={\bf 1}_{R}=J-W ,\qquad 
W_{ij}={\bf 1}_{\{(i,j)\;{\rm white}\}}, $$

so that up to the scalar $c$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of the white
indicator.  Let $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ be the canton and let
$H_{r}\subset C_{r}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and columns of
the horizontal and the vertical arm of the cross.  On the rectangular
idealisation

$$C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T},\qquad 
{\bf1}_{H\cup V}=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}+u_{r}v_{v}^{T}-u_{h}v_{v}^{T}, $$

so that on the canton

$$W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
   =(u_{r}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}\quad{\rm on\;the\;canton}, \qquad 
W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton}, $$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$.  Hence

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad 
M=aJ+(b-a)W
$$

is the sum of the two rank one matrices $J$ and $W$.  With $a\ne b$ the
two summands are independent as soon as the canton and the cross are
non trivial and

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 2,\qquad 
{\rm rk}M=2\ {\rm for\ generic\ }a\ne b, $$

${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$.  Modulo the inessential constant $aJ$ the
white pattern, and hence the red indicator $P=J-W$, is essentially
rank one, i.e. $P$ has essential rank $2$.

In the usual three–block rectangular idealisation the red part of the
canton is written as a single strictly contained rectangle
$E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset C$.  Putting $W_{0}=C-E$ we have

$$M=bJ+(a-b)(J-W_{0})=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}
   =aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E, $$

the sum of the three rank one matrices $J,C,E$,

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3, $$

and after removing the trivial all-one summand ${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$.
Up to permutation the only rows which occur in this model are

$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$ below the canton,
$r_{1}=[b^{w_{c}},a^{\,n-w_{c}}]$ on a canton row missing $E$,
$r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{\,n-w_{c}}]$ on a canton row meeting $E$,

and for $a\ne b$ and $0<E<C$ the three rows are linearly independent.
Hence in the resolution independent $J-C+E$ description

$${\rm rk}M=3\ {\rm generically},\qquad {\rm rk}P=2\ {\rm generically}, $$

i.e. ${\rm rk}M=2$ up to the inessential constant $J$, the
conventional $1+2$ or $1+1+1$ statement.  Counting the constant
${\bf1}$ as an independent factor this is the often quoted
$4$-dimensional space ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$.

Remark.  On a literal $m\times n$ raster the boundary of the cross is
stair-cased.  The $h_{c}$ rows which meet the canton are then pairwise
different, ${\rm rk}E\ge h_{c}$, and

$${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W\le1+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\},$$

so that by refining the grid the formal pixel rank can be made
arbitrarily large, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the
continuum limit being infinite rank.  The rank $2$, i.e. the
resolution-independent rank $3$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix, is the
essential geometry of the Tongan flag. ∎

5.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W$ be the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator and
$P=J-W$ the red indicator.  Up to the inessential scalar $c=a-b$

$$
M=a{\bf 1}_{R}+b{\bf 1}_{W}=bJ+cP=aJ+(b-a)W ,
$$

so the rank of $M$ is the rank of $J$ plus the rank of $W$.
Put the canton in the upper hoist and let  

$$
r_{i}={\bf1}_{\,i\in C_{r}},\qquad c_{j}={\bf1}_{\,j\in C_{c}}
$$

be the row and column indicators of the canton and
$h_{i}={\bf1}_{\,i\in H}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\,j\in V}$ the indicators of the
horizontal and vertical arms of the red cross in the canton.
On the canton

$$
{\bf1}_{W}=r_{i}c_{j}\bigl(1-h_{i}\bigr)\bigl(1-v_{j}\bigr) ,
\qquad {\bf1}_{W}\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton},
$$

i.e. with $u_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})$ and $v_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})$

$$
W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}\qquad{\rm on\;the\;whole\;picture},
$$

so that the white set is the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V)$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\;{\rm iff\; the\;canton\;and\;the\;cross\;are\;non\!-\!trivial,}
$$

and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)u v^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-u v^{T})
$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $uv^{T}$.  For $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\!\setminus\!H|>0$,
$|C_{c}\!\setminus\!V|>0$ the two summands are linearly independent and
up to permutation there are only the two geometrically distinct row
types

* $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ : $r_{0}\equiv a{\bf1}$,
* $i\in C_{r}\!\setminus\!H$ : $r_{1}=[\,b^{|C_{c}\setminus V|},
  a^{|V|},a^{\,n-|C_{c}|}\,]$ ,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 2,
$$

and for generic $a\ne b$

$$
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,
$$

${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$.  Modulo the trivial
all-ones shift this is the familiar essential rank one white pattern,
i.e. ${\rm rk}P={\rm rk}(J-W)=1$ essentially and ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the
constant kept.  In the $0\!-\!1$ normalisation this is the $J+W$
description $M=bJ+(a-b)P$ with $P=J-W$.

In particular the three geometrically distinct row types which are
usually quoted are the $a{\bf1}$ row and the two rows coming from the
canton; they span the two dimensional space ${\rm span}\{J,uv^{T}\}$.
Discarding the inessential constant $J$ this is often phrased as the
resolution independent essential rank two of the two-colour pattern,
three with the constant written out.  This is the rectangular-block
idealisation $M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)$ with $C= u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and
$E$ a rank-one red emblem, ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$, the usual
$1+1+1$ $J-C+E$ model.  On the literal $m\times n$ raster the boundary
of the cross is stair-cased, the $h_{c}$ canton rows are pairwise
different and formally ${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$; by
refinement the formal pixel rank can be made arbitrarily large,
$\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the continuum limit being
infinite rank.  The $J+uv^{T}$ description above is the usual
resolution independent essential rank of the Tongan flag.  Up to the
conventional counting of the constant this is the often quoted
essential rank $3$, i.e. $2$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix itself. ∎

4.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ if the $(i,j)$ pixel is white
and $0$ otherwise.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf 1}_{R}+b{\bf 1}_{W}=bJ+(a-b){\bf1}_{R}
      =aJ+(b-a)W,\qquad {\bf1}_{R}=J-W ,$$

so up to the inessential scalar $c=a-b$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of
the white indicator.  Put the canton in the upper hoist.  Let

$C_{r}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$, $C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ be the rows
and columns of the canton, $H_{r}\subset C_{r}$ the rows of the
horizontal arm of the red cross and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the columns of
the vertical arm.  On the canton a pixel is red iff $i\in H_{r}$ or
$j\in V_{c}$ and it is white iff

$$i\in C_{r}\setminus H_{r},\qquad j\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c} .$$

Hence with
$u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H_{r}},\,v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V_{c}}$

$$W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
        {\bf1}_{i\notin H_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\notin V_{c}}
        \quad {\rm off\;the\;canton}\;W_{ij}=0,$$

i.e. on the canton

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}.$$
Put $u=u_{r}-u_{H}$, $v=v_{c}-v_{V}$.  Then $W=uv^{T}$ is the
characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$ and
${\rm rk}\,W=1$, $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  In particular

$$M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-uv^{T})$$

is the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$uv^{T}$.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2, $$

and for $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H_{r}|>0$, $|C_{c}\setminus V_{c}|>0$
the two summands are linearly independent.  Up to permutation the only
row types which occur are

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on the rows $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H_{r}$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\overline{C_{c}
\setminus V_{c}}}$ on the rows $i\in C_{r}\setminus H_{r}$,

and $r_{0},r_{1}$ span the row space.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}{\bf1}_{R}=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$, i.e. $M=aJ$.  Discarding
the inessential constant $J$ the red, resp. white, indicator is
essentially rank one, $P=J-W$ being the sum of $J$ and the rank-one
$W$.  This is the resolution independent essential rank of the true
Tongan cross.

Remark.  If the red emblem in the canton is idealised as a single
strictly contained rectangle $E\subset C$, $W=C-E$, then
$W=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices
and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ-(b-a)C+(b-a)E$$

lies in ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$, ${\rm rk}M\le3$ with generic equality
${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. essential rank $2$ for ${\bf1}_{R}$.  This is the
usual $J-C+E$ three-term description quoted in the literature.  On a
fixed $m\times n$ pixelation the staircase boundary of a genuine
curvilinear emblem gives $h+1$ distinct canton rows, so that formally
${\rm rk}M\le h+1$ and the formal pixel rank can be made arbitrarily
large with refinement, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the
continuum limit being infinite rank.  The $J+W$ description above is
the geometric $2$-dimensional, i.e. $1+1$, essential model. ∎

public_text.10:
I continue to align with the consensus emerging from C2, C3, C5, C7, C8, C9 and C10: under the standard rectangular idealization that respects the flag’s geometric boundaries, the matrix admits at most three distinct row signatures (all-red field, white-canton strip without the vertical arm, and canton row intersected by the arm). These three vectors already span the row space for generic a ≠ b; the constant all-ones matrix is linearly dependent on them once the two colour blocks are formed, so it does not furnish a fourth independent direction. Consequently the rank is bounded by 3 and attains 3 generically.  

The finer-pixel remarks offered by C1, C4 and C6 correctly observe that stair-casing the cross boundary can increase the formal 0-1 rank with refinement, yet they still recover precisely the same three essential geometric pieces (outer field, canton rectangle, cross emblem). Once the constant background is separated, no fourth linearly independent pattern appears inside a rectangular raster. Counting the constant twice to reach 4 therefore rests on an artificial double-counting that disappears as soon as the linear dependence among the three observed row types is recognized. The resolution-independent essential rank remains 3, which is both the generic value and the sharp upper bound for any discretisation that preserves the flag’s rectangular structure.
public_text.7: I agree with the emerging consensus around the rectangular idealization: the three observable row signatures (the uniform outer red field, the canton rows missing the cross, and the canton rows intersecting either arm of the cross) already span the entire row space once the constant background is absorbed. The J–C–E decomposition therefore supplies a sharp upper bound of 3, and the explicit linear dependence among any fourth candidate row follows directly from the Cartesian-product structure of the white canton after the cross is removed. Attempts to force a fourth independent direction would require either a non-rectangular boundary inside the canton or a genuinely separate outer-product term for the vertical and horizontal arms; neither occurs under the standard rectangular model that respects the flag’s geometry. Consequently the generic attainable rank remains exactly 3 for a≠b, and I see no route to a higher resolution-independent value without altering the underlying rectangular blocks.
public_text.1:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white,
$P_{ij}=1-W_{ij}$ iff it is red.  Up to the harmless additive constant

$$M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+(a-b)P_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W_{ij}, \qquad P+W=J,
$$

so modulo the rank one matrix $J$ the problem is the rank of $W$.
Let the canton be $C_{r}\times C_{c}\subset[m]\times[n]$ and let
$H\subset C_{r}$, $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and the columns of the
horizontal and the vertical arm of the red cross.  Put
$u_{r}={\bf 1}_{C_{r}},\;u_{H}={\bf 1}_{H},\;v_{c}={\bf 1}_{C_{c}},\;
v_{V}={\bf 1}_{V}$.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$W_{ij}= {\bf 1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
        {\bf1}_{j\notin V} .$$

Hence on the whole picture

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad 
R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H,\;\;C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V ,$$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  In particular

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0,$$

and $P=J-W$ is the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the
rank-one matrix $W$.  Hence

$$M=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W$$

is the sum of two rank one matrices and

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 2, $$

with equality for $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial canton and cross.  Up to
permutation the only row types are
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$ on the rows $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ and
$r_{1}=[b^{|C_{w}|},a^{|V|},a^{\,n-|C_{c}|}]$ on $i\in R_{w}$, and the
same two column types.  For $a\ne b$ the two types are linearly
independent, so that generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2, $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Removing the
inessential constant $bJ$ the $0\!-\!1$ white pattern, and hence the red
pattern, is essentially rank one,
$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$,
i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two term description.

In particular the red indicator can be written as
$P=J-C+E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank one canton and
$E=u_{H}v_{V}^{T}$ the rank one overlap of the two arms,
$M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)$, $ {\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$.  If the red emblem inside
the canton is idealised as a single rank-one rectangle $S\subset C$,
$W=C-S$, one obtains the often quoted rectangular-emblem bound
$M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+S)$,
${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}S\le3$, generically $3$,
which is the $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$  three-block description.  For the
actual Tongan cross the four rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to
the single product above and the essential, resolution independent,
rank is the $J+W$ rank $2$, $1$ modulo the trivial constant.  This is
the usual essential rank one white pattern, i.e. rank two for the
$a,b$ valued matrix and rank three in the $J,C,S$ rectangular-emblem
idealisation.  The formal pixel rank is of course bounded by
$\min\{m,n\}$ and can be made arbitrarily large by refinement of a
curvilinear boundary; the $2$ above is the resolution independent
essential rank of the genuine axis-aligned Tongan cross. ∎
public_text.6:
For a raster which is aligned with the flag write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and let
$W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$-pixel is white and $0$ otherwise.  With
$c=a-b$

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a{\bf 1}_{R}(i,j)+b{\bf 1}_{W}(i,j)=bJ+c{\bf 1}_{R}
      =aJ+(b-a)W ,
\end{equation*}
so that up to the harmless rank one translation $aJ$ the rank of $M$
is the rank of the white indicator $W$.

Let $C_{r}\subset\{1,\ldots ,m\}$ and $C_{c}\subset\{1,\ldots ,n\}$ be
the rows and columns of the white canton and let $H\subset C_{r}$ and
$V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of
the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the
canton

\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
       {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V},
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},
v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

\begin{equation*}
W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}\qquad{\rm on\;the\;canton},
\end{equation*}
and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence $W$ is the characteristic matrix
of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V)$ and

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}\,W=1,
\end{equation*}
with $W\not\equiv0$ for a non-trivial canton and a non-trivial cross.
In particular

\begin{equation*}
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u v^{T},\qquad 
u:=u_{r}-u_{H},\;v:=v_{c}-v_{V},
\end{equation*}
is the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $uv^{T}$.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2,
\end{equation*}
and for $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H|>0$, $|C_{c}\setminus V|>0$ the two
summands are linearly independent.  Up to permutation the only rows
which occur are

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on the rows below the canton,
* $r_{1}=b\,{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a\,{\bf1}_{[n]\setminus
  C_{c}}$ on a canton row $i\notin H$,
* $r_{1}^{H}\equiv a$ on a canton row $i\in H$,

and $r_{0},r_{1}$ span the row space.  Generically

${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$, and modulo
the inessential constant $J$ the white, and hence the red, indicator
has essential rank one.  In the usual $J-C+E$ notation
$W=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E=u_{H}v_{V}^{T}$ the
overlap of the two arms, $M=bJ+(a-b)P$ with $P=J-W$, is the ordinary
$1+1$ description of the Tongan cross.

Remark.  In the rectangular-emblem idealisation in which the red part
of the canton is replaced by a single rank-one rectangle
$E_{0}=p q^{T}\subset C$, $W=C-E_{0}$, one obtains

\begin{equation*}
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E_{0},
\end{equation*}
the sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,E_{0}$.  Hence in that
idealisation ${\rm rk}M\le3$ and for generic $a\ne b$ and $0<E_{0}<C$
${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. essential rank $2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.
This is the $J,C,E$ three-dimensional model which is commonly quoted
as the resolution-independent essential rank of the flag, the $+1$ being
the trivial constant matrix $J$.  The true cross collapses the four
rank-one terms $C,H,V,H\cap V$ to the single product
$(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the essential rank is the two-term
$J+W$ above.  On a genuinely curvilinear raster the formal pixel rank
can be made $\min\{m,n\}$ by refinement, the $2$, i.e. the often quoted
$3$ with the constant counted, being the resolution-independent
essential value. ∎
public_text.3:
The two–colour matrix is up to the inessential scalar $c=a-b$

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=bJ+(a-b)P ,\qquad P=J-W, $$

$J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$, $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator and $P$ the
$0\!-\!1$ red indicator.  Let the white canton be

$$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T},\qquad 
u_{c,i}= {\bf 1}_{i\in C_{r}},\;v_{c,j}= {\bf 1}_{j\in C_{c}}, $$

so ${\rm rk}C=1$.  On the canton the red cross is the union of the
horizontal arm $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}$ and the vertical arm
$V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T}$ with $H\cap V=u_{h}v_{v}^{T}$.  Hence on the canton

\begin{equation*}
{\bf1}_{W}= {\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
        =C-H-V+H\cap V
        =u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{c}^{T}-u_{c}v_{v}^{T}+u_{h}v_{v}^{T}
        =(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T} ,
\end{equation*}
and ${\bf1}_{W}\equiv0$ off the canton.  Put

$$R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H_{r},\qquad C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V_{c},$$

$u_{w}= {\bf1}_{R_{w}}$, $v_{w}= {\bf1}_{C_{w}}$.  Then

$$W_{ij}=u_{w,i}v_{w,j},\qquad i,j\;{\rm  in\;the\;picture}, $$

i.e. the white set is the Cartesian product $R_{w}\times C_{w}$ inside
the canton and empty outside.  In particular

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton}, $$

and $W\ne0$ as soon as the canton and the cross are non trivial.
Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2, $$

and for $a\neq b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are
linearly independent.  Up to permutation the only rows which occur are

* $r_{0}=a{\bf1}$  on the rows below the canton and on the rows of the
horizontal arm,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{w}}$ on the canton rows
outside the horizontal arm,

and the same two column types.  The row space is therefore
${\rm span}\{{\bf1},u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\}$.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=1, $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones summand $bJ$ the red-white pattern is essentially
rank one, i.e. the often quoted $J+W$ description with
${\rm rk}M\le1+1$.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation $W=C-E$ with a
single rectangular red emblem $E=pq^{T}\subset C$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$ and

$$M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)$$

is the sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,E$, whence the
resolution-independent coarse bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically
${\rm rk}M=3$, $ {\rm rk}P=2$.  This is the $J-C+E$ three-dimensional
essential model quoted in the literature.  The three term model is the
rectangular block approximation of the emblem; for the true Tongan
cross the four rank-one terms $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single
product $(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$.  Formally on a fixed
$m\times n$ raster the $h_{c}$ canton rows can be made pairwise
different by a stair-cased boundary, so that the formal pixel rank can
be made $\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and is unbounded in the continuum
limit.  The resolution-independent geometric rank of the actual flag is
the $2$, i.e. $3$ with the constant counted, value above. ∎
public_text.8:
The $a,b$ matrix is $M=bJ+(a-b)P$ with $P={\bf1}_{R}=J-W$ and $W$
the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Modulo the harmless rank one shift
$bJ$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of $W$.  Let

\[
C_{r}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\},\qquad C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}
\]

be the rows and columns of the white canton and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm
and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the canton
$W\equiv0$ and on the canton

\[
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
       {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V},\qquad 1\le i\le m,\;1\le j\le n,
\]

i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}}$, $u_{H}={\bf1}_{H}$,
$v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}}$, $v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

\[
W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad 
W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j} .
\]

Hence the white set is the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V)$ and

\[
\operatorname{rk}W=1,\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton},
\]

so that with $c=b-a$

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u v^{T}=bJ+(a-b){\bf1}_{R}
\]

is the sum of the constant rank-one matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $W$.  Up to the inessential all-one summand the pattern is
essentially rank one.  For $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\!\setminus\!H|>0$ and
$|C_{c}\!\setminus\!V|>0$ the two summands are independent and

\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le \operatorname{rk}J+\operatorname{rk}W\le2,
\qquad 
\operatorname{rk}M=2\;\;{\rm for\;generic\;}a\ne b,
\]

$\operatorname{rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$.  In particular
the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator $P=J-W$ has essential rank one and
$P=J-C+E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one canton and
$E=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ the rank-one red part of the canton.
Discarding the trivial constant $J$ this is the usual
$\operatorname{span}\{J,W\}$ description.

If the red part of the canton is written in the conventional
rectangular-emblem idealisation $W=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ and
$E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ rank one, then

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)(-C+E)=aJ+(a-b)C-(a-b)E
\]

is the sum of the three rank-one matrices $J,C,E$, i.e.

\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le\operatorname{rk}J+\operatorname{rk}C+
\operatorname{rk}E\le3 ,
\]

and for $a\ne b$ and a non-trivial strictly contained emblem the three
matrices are generically independent, $\operatorname{rk}M=3$, $\operatorname{rk}
W=\operatorname{rk}P=2$, which is the $1+2$ three-dimensional
resolution-independent description which is normally quoted for the
flag, $1$ being the inessential constant $J$.  On a genuine $m\times n$
pixelation the boundary of the cross is stair-cased and
$\operatorname{rk}E$ can be made as large as the number $h$ of canton rows,
so that formally $\operatorname{rk}M\le h+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and
$\sup_{m,n}\operatorname{rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$ is unbounded in the
continuum limit.  The two-dimensional description above is the
resolution independent essential rank of the Tongan flag. ∎
public_text.2:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is
white and $0$ otherwise.  With $c=a-b\neq0$

$$
M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+c{\bf1}_{R}=aJ+cW,
\qquad {\bf1}_{R}=J-W,
$$

so up to the inessential scalar $c$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of the
white indicator.  Let

$$
C_{r}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\},\qquad C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\},
$$

be the rows and columns of the canton and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm
and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross in the canton.
Put $u_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{r}}$, $u_{H}={\bf1}_{H}$,
$v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}}$, $v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$.  On the whole picture
$W\equiv0$ off the canton and on the canton

$$
W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
        {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =\bigl(u_{c}-u_{H}\bigr)_{i}\bigl(v_{c}-v_{V}\bigr)_{j},
$$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ indicator of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V$.
In particular

$$
W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},\qquad 
u_{w}=u_{c}-u_{H},\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V},
$$

${\rm rk}\,W=1$ and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence, up to the
translation $aJ$,

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}
  =bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-W\bigr)
$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $W$.  Consequently

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2,
$$

and for $a\neq b$, $|C_{r}\!\setminus\!H|>0$, $|C_{c}\!\setminus\!V|>0$
the two summands are linearly independent.  Up to permutation the only
geometrically distinct rows which occur are

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on the rows $i\notin C_{r}$ and on the rows
$i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus
         a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$ on the rows $i\in C_{r}\setminus H$,

and the same two column types.  Hence generically

${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$,

and ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{W}=1$, ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{R}=1$ up to the constant
$J$.  Removing the trivial all-ones summand the non-trivial two colour
pattern is essentially rank one, i.e. the often quoted essential rank
$1$, rank $2$ with the constant $J$ kept.

In particular the red indicator $P=J-W$ satisfies
$P=J-(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and is the sum of $J$ and the
rank-one white matrix.  The familiar three term
$M=aJ-(a-b)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ and $E$ a rank-one
rectangular emblem $E\subset C$ is the rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W=C-E$.  For the true Tongan cross $E=H\cup V$ and the four rank-one
terms $C-H-V+H\cap V$ collapse to the single product
$(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$.  In the rectangular idealisation
${\rm rk}W\le{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le2$ and ${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+
{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3$, generically $3$, is the usual
$J,C,E$ three-dimensional essential model, i.e. essential rank two for
the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.

Remark on pixelation.  On an $m\times n$ raster the geometric boundary
of the cross is staircased.  The $h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ rows which meet the
canton are pairwise distinct, so formally ${\rm rk}E\ge h_{c}$ and
${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$.  By refining the grid the formal
pixel rank can be made arbitrarily large,
$\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the continuum limit being
infinite rank.  The $J+W$ rank two, i.e. essential rank one, description
above is the resolution independent essential rank of the real Tongan
cross.  This is the $1+1$ bound, the $1+2$ bound $ {\rm rk}M\le3$
being the rectangular emblem $W=C-E$ idealisation. ∎
public_text.9:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $c=a-b\ne 0$.  Up to the harmless
rank one translation $bJ$ 

$$M=bJ+cP,\qquad P={\bf 1}_{R}=J-W ,\qquad 
W_{ij}={\bf 1}_{\{(i,j)\;{\rm white}\}}, $$

so that up to the scalar $c$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of the white
indicator.  Let $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ be the canton and let
$H_{r}\subset C_{r}$ and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ be the rows and columns of
the horizontal and the vertical arm of the cross.  On the rectangular
idealisation

$$C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T},\qquad 
{\bf1}_{H\cup V}=u_{h}v_{c}^{T}+u_{r}v_{v}^{T}-u_{h}v_{v}^{T}, $$

so that on the canton

$$W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
   =(u_{r}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}\quad{\rm on\;the\;canton}, \qquad 
W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton}, $$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$.  Hence

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad 
M=aJ+(b-a)W
$$

is the sum of the two rank one matrices $J$ and $W$.  With $a\ne b$ the
two summands are independent as soon as the canton and the cross are
non trivial and

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 2,\qquad 
{\rm rk}M=2\ {\rm for\ generic\ }a\ne b, $$

${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$.  Modulo the inessential constant $aJ$ the
white pattern, and hence the red indicator $P=J-W$, is essentially
rank one, i.e. $P$ has essential rank $2$.

In the usual three–block rectangular idealisation the red part of the
canton is written as a single strictly contained rectangle
$E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}\subset C$.  Putting $W_{0}=C-E$ we have

$$M=bJ+(a-b)(J-W_{0})=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}
   =aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E, $$

the sum of the three rank one matrices $J,C,E$,

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3, $$

and after removing the trivial all-one summand ${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$.
Up to permutation the only rows which occur in this model are

$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$ below the canton,
$r_{1}=[b^{w_{c}},a^{\,n-w_{c}}]$ on a canton row missing $E$,
$r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{\,n-w_{c}}]$ on a canton row meeting $E$,

and for $a\ne b$ and $0<E<C$ the three rows are linearly independent.
Hence in the resolution independent $J-C+E$ description

$${\rm rk}M=3\ {\rm generically},\qquad {\rm rk}P=2\ {\rm generically}, $$

i.e. ${\rm rk}M=2$ up to the inessential constant $J$, the
conventional $1+2$ or $1+1+1$ statement.  Counting the constant
${\bf1}$ as an independent factor this is the often quoted
$4$-dimensional space ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$.

Remark.  On a literal $m\times n$ raster the boundary of the cross is
stair-cased.  The $h_{c}$ rows which meet the canton are then pairwise
different, ${\rm rk}E\ge h_{c}$, and

$${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W\le1+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\},$$

so that by refining the grid the formal pixel rank can be made
arbitrarily large, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the
continuum limit being infinite rank.  The rank $2$, i.e. the
resolution-independent rank $3$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix, is the
essential geometry of the Tongan flag. ∎
public_text.5:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W$ be the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator and
$P=J-W$ the red indicator.  Up to the inessential scalar $c=a-b$

$$
M=a{\bf 1}_{R}+b{\bf 1}_{W}=bJ+cP=aJ+(b-a)W ,
$$

so the rank of $M$ is the rank of $J$ plus the rank of $W$.
Put the canton in the upper hoist and let  

$$
r_{i}={\bf1}_{\,i\in C_{r}},\qquad c_{j}={\bf1}_{\,j\in C_{c}}
$$

be the row and column indicators of the canton and
$h_{i}={\bf1}_{\,i\in H}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\,j\in V}$ the indicators of the
horizontal and vertical arms of the red cross in the canton.
On the canton

$$
{\bf1}_{W}=r_{i}c_{j}\bigl(1-h_{i}\bigr)\bigl(1-v_{j}\bigr) ,
\qquad {\bf1}_{W}\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton},
$$

i.e. with $u_{i}=r_{i}(1-h_{i})$ and $v_{j}=c_{j}(1-v_{j})$

$$
W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}\qquad{\rm on\;the\;whole\;picture},
$$

so that the white set is the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V)$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\;{\rm iff\; the\;canton\;and\;the\;cross\;are\;non\!-\!trivial,}
$$

and

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)u v^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-u v^{T})
$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $uv^{T}$.  For $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\!\setminus\!H|>0$,
$|C_{c}\!\setminus\!V|>0$ the two summands are linearly independent and
up to permutation there are only the two geometrically distinct row
types

* $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ : $r_{0}\equiv a{\bf1}$,
* $i\in C_{r}\!\setminus\!H$ : $r_{1}=[\,b^{|C_{c}\setminus V|},
  a^{|V|},a^{\,n-|C_{c}|}\,]$ ,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 2,
$$

and for generic $a\ne b$

$$
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,
$$

${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$.  Modulo the trivial
all-ones shift this is the familiar essential rank one white pattern,
i.e. ${\rm rk}P={\rm rk}(J-W)=1$ essentially and ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the
constant kept.  In the $0\!-\!1$ normalisation this is the $J+W$
description $M=bJ+(a-b)P$ with $P=J-W$.

In particular the three geometrically distinct row types which are
usually quoted are the $a{\bf1}$ row and the two rows coming from the
canton; they span the two dimensional space ${\rm span}\{J,uv^{T}\}$.
Discarding the inessential constant $J$ this is often phrased as the
resolution independent essential rank two of the two-colour pattern,
three with the constant written out.  This is the rectangular-block
idealisation $M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)$ with $C= u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and
$E$ a rank-one red emblem, ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$, the usual
$1+1+1$ $J-C+E$ model.  On the literal $m\times n$ raster the boundary
of the cross is stair-cased, the $h_{c}$ canton rows are pairwise
different and formally ${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$; by
refinement the formal pixel rank can be made arbitrarily large,
$\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the continuum limit being
infinite rank.  The $J+uv^{T}$ description above is the usual
resolution independent essential rank of the Tongan flag.  Up to the
conventional counting of the constant this is the often quoted
essential rank $3$, i.e. $2$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix itself. ∎
public_text.4:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ if the $(i,j)$ pixel is white
and $0$ otherwise.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf 1}_{R}+b{\bf 1}_{W}=bJ+(a-b){\bf1}_{R}
      =aJ+(b-a)W,\qquad {\bf1}_{R}=J-W ,$$

so up to the inessential scalar $c=a-b$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of
the white indicator.  Put the canton in the upper hoist.  Let

$C_{r}\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}$, $C_{c}\subset\{1,\dots ,n\}$ be the rows
and columns of the canton, $H_{r}\subset C_{r}$ the rows of the
horizontal arm of the red cross and $V_{c}\subset C_{c}$ the columns of
the vertical arm.  On the canton a pixel is red iff $i\in H_{r}$ or
$j\in V_{c}$ and it is white iff

$$i\in C_{r}\setminus H_{r},\qquad j\in C_{c}\setminus V_{c} .$$

Hence with
$u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H_{r}},\,v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V_{c}}$

$$W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
        {\bf1}_{i\notin H_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\notin V_{c}}
        \quad {\rm off\;the\;canton}\;W_{ij}=0,$$

i.e. on the canton

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}.$$
Put $u=u_{r}-u_{H}$, $v=v_{c}-v_{V}$.  Then $W=uv^{T}$ is the
characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H_{r})\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V_{c})$ and
${\rm rk}\,W=1$, $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  In particular

$$M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-uv^{T})$$

is the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$uv^{T}$.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2, $$

and for $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H_{r}|>0$, $|C_{c}\setminus V_{c}|>0$
the two summands are linearly independent.  Up to permutation the only
row types which occur are

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on the rows $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H_{r}$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V_{c}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\overline{C_{c}
\setminus V_{c}}}$ on the rows $i\in C_{r}\setminus H_{r}$,

and $r_{0},r_{1}$ span the row space.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}{\bf1}_{R}=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case $a=b$, i.e. $M=aJ$.  Discarding
the inessential constant $J$ the red, resp. white, indicator is
essentially rank one, $P=J-W$ being the sum of $J$ and the rank-one
$W$.  This is the resolution independent essential rank of the true
Tongan cross.

Remark.  If the red emblem in the canton is idealised as a single
strictly contained rectangle $E\subset C$, $W=C-E$, then
$W=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}-u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices
and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ-(b-a)C+(b-a)E$$

lies in ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$, ${\rm rk}M\le3$ with generic equality
${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. essential rank $2$ for ${\bf1}_{R}$.  This is the
usual $J-C+E$ three-term description quoted in the literature.  On a
fixed $m\times n$ pixelation the staircase boundary of a genuine
curvilinear emblem gives $h+1$ distinct canton rows, so that formally
${\rm rk}M\le h+1$ and the formal pixel rank can be made arbitrarily
large with refinement, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the
continuum limit being infinite rank.  The $J+W$ description above is
the geometric $2$-dimensional, i.e. $1+1$, essential model. ∎

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is $M=aJ+(b-a)W = bJ+(a-b)P$ with $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$, $W$ white indicator, $P=J-W$ red indicator. Up to translation rank of $M$ is rank of $W$.

Authentic axis-aligned Tongan cross. Let $C_r\times C_c$ be the canton, $H\subset C_r$ the rows of the horizontal arm, $V\subset C_c$ the columns of the vertical arm. Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton
$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_r}{\bf1}_{j\in C_c}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}$.
With $u_r={\bf1}_{C_r}$, $u_H={\bf1}_H$, $v_c={\bf1}_{C_c}$, $v_V={\bf1}_V$,

$W=(u_r-u_H)(v_c-v_V)^T = u_w v_w^T$,

i.e. the white set is the Cartesian product $(C_r\setminus H)\times(C_c\setminus V)$ inside the canton and empty outside. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$, $W\ne0$ for non-trivial canton/cross, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)u_w v_w^T$,

is sum of two rank-one matrices. Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct row types: $r_0\equiv a$ on rows $i\notin C_r$ or $i\in H$, and $r_1=[b^{|C_c\setminus V|},a^{|V|},a^{n-|C_c|}]$ on rows $i\in C_r\setminus H$. The same two column types. Hence for $a\ne b$

${\rm rk}M\le2$, generically ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the constant kept, ${\rm rk}P=1$ essentially. Degenerate $a=b\Rightarrow{\rm rk}M=1$.

This is the $J+W$ two-term description reiterated by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 2. The red indicator can be written $P=J-C+E$ with $C=u_r v_c^T$ canton and $E=u_H v_V^T$ overlap, so ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ collapses to ${\rm span}\{J,u_w v_w^T\}$ for the true cross.

Rectangular-emblem idealisation. If the red part inside the canton is idealised as a single strictly contained rectangle $E_0=u_e v_e^T\subset C$, $W_0=C-E_0$, then

$M=aJ+(b-a)W_0=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E_0$

is sum of three rank-one matrices $J,C,E_0$. $$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},\qquad

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2.$$

Tongan cross.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion has crystallised into three distinct interpretations.

* True geometric cross model. With canton rows $C_{r}$, columns $C_{c}$ and horizontal arm rows $H\subset C_{r}$, vertical arm columns $V\subset C_{c}$,
