* Pixel refinement / continuum limit. On a genuine $m\times n$ raster the emblem boundary is staircased. On the $h$ canton rows the row sections are distinct, so formally ${\rm rk}E\ge h$ and ${\rm rk}M\le h+1\le\min\{m,n\}$. By refining the grid the formal rank can be made arbitrarily large, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, infinite in the continuum limit. This unboundedness is repeatedly noted by Colleagues 1,4,6.

Current tension therefore remains:
– geometric cross: essential rank one for $W$, rank two for the $a,b$-valued matrix $M$, the $J+W$ bound;
– rectangular emblem idealisation: essential rank two for $W$, rank three for $M$, the usual $J-C+E$ bound quoted in the literature;
– formal pixel rank unbounded with resolution.

The problem is $M=aJ+(b-a)W = bJ+(a-b)P$ with $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$, $W$ white indicator, $P=J-W$ red indicator. Up to translation rank of $M$ is rank of $W$.

Authentic axis-aligned Tongan cross. Let $C_r\times C_c$ be the canton, $H\subset C_r$ the rows of the horizontal arm, $V\subset C_c$ the columns of the vertical arm. Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton
$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_r}{\bf1}_{j\in C_c}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}$.
With $u_r={\bf1}_{C_r}$, $u_H={\bf1}_H$, $v_c={\bf1}_{C_c}$, $v_V={\bf1}_V$,

$W=(u_r-u_H)(v_c-v_V)^T = u_w v_w^T$,

i.e. the white set is the Cartesian product $(C_r\setminus H)\times(C_c\setminus V)$ inside the canton and empty outside. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$, $W\ne0$ for non-trivial canton/cross, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)u_w v_w^T$,

is sum of two rank-one matrices. Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct row types: $r_0\equiv a$ on rows $i\notin C_r$ or $i\in H$, and $r_1=[b^{|C_c\setminus V|},a^{|V|},a^{n-|C_c|}]$ on rows $i\in C_r\setminus H$. The same two column types. Hence for $a\ne b$

${\rm rk}M\le2$, generically ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the constant kept, ${\rm rk}P=1$ essentially. Degenerate $a=b\Rightarrow{\rm rk}M=1$.

This is the $J+W$ two-term description reiterated by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 2. The red indicator can be written $P=J-C+E$ with $C=u_r v_c^T$ canton and $E=u_H v_V^T$ overlap, so ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ collapses to ${\rm span}\{J,u_w v_w^T\}$ for the true cross.

Rectangular-emblem idealisation. If the red part inside the canton is idealised as a single strictly contained rectangle $E_0=u_e v_e^T\subset C$, $W_0=C-E_0$, then

$M=aJ+(b-a)W_0=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E_0$

is sum of three rank-one matrices $J,C,E_0$. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le3$, and for generic $a\ne b$, $0<E_0<C$ the three rows $r_0=a{\bf1}$, $r_1=[b^{w_c},a^{n-w_c}]$, $r_2=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{n-w_c}]$ are independent, so generic ${\rm rk}M=3$, essential rank $2$ for $P$. Formal pixel rank. On a literal $m\times n$ raster the staircased boundary of a curvilinear emblem gives $h_c=|C_r|$ distinct canton rows, so formally ${\rm rk}M\le h_c+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$ is unbounded in the continuum limit. The $J+W$ rank 2 is resolution-independent essential rank; the $h_c+1$ bound is the formal pixel rank.

Current disagreement remains: strict geometry of the Tongan cross gives generic rank 2 for the $a,b$-valued matrix, rank 1 modulo the constant. The literature-quoted rectangular emblem idealisation gives generic rank 3, i.e. essential rank 2 for $P$. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 hold the authentic rank-2 view in round 2; Colleagues 7,10 hold the rectangular-idealisation rank-3 view. reflection_text.1:
The flag is red field with a white canton in the upper hoist and a red cross inside the canton.  Modulo the harmless rank-one shift $bJ$ the problem is the rank of the white indicator $W$.

Let $C_{r},C_{c}$ be the rows/columns of the canton and $H\subset C_{r}$, $V\subset C_{c}$ the rows of the horizontal arm and columns of the vertical arm of the cross.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}.$$

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},\qquad 
R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H,\;C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V,$$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product $R_{w}\times C_{w}$ and is $0$ off the canton. Hence ${\rm rk}\,W=1$ for a non-trivial canton and cross, $W\neq0$ iff $|R_{w}|>0,|C_{w}|>0$.

With $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$,

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W,$$
$P=J-W$, so

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T})$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white matrix $W$.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2.$$

Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct row types,
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$ on rows $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$, and
$r_{1}=[b^{|C_{w}|},a^{|V|},a^{\,n-|C_{c}|}]$ on $i\in R_{w}$, and the
same two column types.  For $a\neq b$ and $|R_{w}|,|C_{w}|>0$ the two
summands are independent, so generically

${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the constant kept,
${\rm rk}P=1$ essentially, and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate case
$a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Modulo the trivial all-ones shift the red/white pattern
is essentially rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.

This is the $J+W$ resolution-independent essential description.  It
can be written as $M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one
canton and $E=u_{H}v_{V}^{T}$ the overlap of the two arms, i.e.
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$.  The four rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse
to the single product $(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ for the true
Tongan cross.

The rectangular-emblem idealisation $W_{0}=C-E_{0}$ with a single
rank-one rectangle $E_{0}=pq^{T}\subset C$ gives
$M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E_{0}$, the sum of three rank-one
matrices $J,C,E_{0}$, whence the often quoted coarse bound
${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically ${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. essential rank $2$ for
the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.  Colleagues 10 and 7 maintain the $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$
three-block rank $3$ statement; colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 point out the
collapse to the $J+W$ two-term description and the generic rank $2$.

Formal pixel rank is not resolution independent.  On an $m\times n$
raster the stair-cased boundary of a curvilinear emblem makes the
$h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ canton rows pairwise distinct, so formally
${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}
=\min\{m,n\}$; in the continuum limit the rank is unbounded.  The
essential geometric rank of the genuine axis-aligned Tongan cross is the
$J+W$ rank $2$, $1$ modulo the constant, commonly quoted as essential
rank $1$ for the $0\!-\!1$ pattern and rank $3$ for the $J,C,E$
rectangular-emblem idealisation. ∎
reflection_text.3:
The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{T}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator, $M=bJ+(a-b)P$, $P=J-W$, so up to the inessential scalar $a-b$ the rank is that of $W$ and of $P$.

For the true axis-aligned Tongan cross let $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ be the white canton and $H\subset C_{r}$, $V\subset C_{c}$ the rows and columns of the horizontal and vertical arms. On the canton

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}, $$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton. With $u_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

$$W=(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},$$

i.e. $W$ is the characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$.
Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ on the canton and $0$ off it, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the constant kept.

Thus

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T})$$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices. Up to permutation the only row types are
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$ on rows $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ and
$r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{w}}$ on rows $i\in R_{w}$.
For $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0,|C_{w}|>0$

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2,\qquad {\rm rk}M=2,$$
${\rm rk}M=1$ for the degenerate $a=b$. Modulo the trivial all-ones summand the
white, and hence the red, pattern is essentially rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation the red part of the canton is
written as a single rank-one rectangle $S\subset C$, $W_{0}=C-S$, $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$,
${\rm rk}C={\rm rk}S=1$. Then

$$M=aJ+(b-a)(C-S)=aJ+(a-b)(-C+S)$$

lies in ${\rm span}\{J,C,S\}$,
${\rm rk}M\le1+1+1=3$, generically ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$, i.e.
essential rank $2$ for $P$, three distinct row signatures
$r_{0}=a{\bf1},r_{1}=[b^{w},a^{n-w}],r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{n-w}]$.
This is the $J-C+E$ three-dimensional description repeatedly quoted as
‘rank 3, 4 counting the constant’.

Formal pixel rank. On a fixed $m\times n$ raster the boundary of a genuinely
curvilinear emblem has $h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ distinct canton rows, so formally
${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and the supremum over refinements is
unbounded. For the axis-aligned Tongan cross the product structure persists under
refinement, so the formal rank stays $2$; the $h+1$ unboundedness is the
stair-case effect for a curvilinear emblem, not for the rectangular cross.

Current status. R2 C1,C2,C3,C4,C5,C6,C8,C9 now derive the strict product
$(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$ and the resolution-independent essential rank
$2$ for $M$, $1$ modulo $J$. C7,C10 still defend the rectangular-emblem
idealisation and quote generic maximal $3$, essentially $2$. The disagreement
is therefore model choice: strict geometric cross $\Rightarrow$ ${\rm rk}M_{\max}=2$
generically, $1$ degenerate; rectangular-emblem idealisation $\Rightarrow$
${\rm rk}M_{\max}=3$, $2$ essentially, often written $4$ with the constant
counted. The unresolved question is which geometric model the problem setter
intends; the mathematically accurate axis-aligned geometry gives the $J+W$ rank-two
bound. ∎

reflection_text.2:

and
$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T})$
is the sum of two rank-one matrices.

Current status.
Geometrically essential rank for the real Tongan cross is $2$ for $M$, $1$ for $W$, i.e. $1$ essential non-trivial modulo $J$. The widely quoted $3$-bound is the rectangular-emblem idealisation $W=C-E$. Formal pixel rank is unbounded with refinement. * True geometric cross model. With canton rows $C_{r}$, columns $C_{c}$ and horizontal arm rows $H\subset C_{r}$, vertical arm columns $V\subset C_{c}$,
$W_{ij}=1_{i\in C_{r}}1_{j\in C_{c}}1_{i\notin H}1_{j\notin V}$ off canton $0$, so
$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ is the indicator of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\setminus H)\times(C_{c}\setminus V)$. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ and
$M=aJ+(b-a)W=bJ+(a-b)(J-W)$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices.
Up to permutation there are only two row types: $r_{0}\equiv a$ on rows
$i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ and $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\overline{C_{c}\setminus V}}$ on $i\in C_{r}\setminus H$.
For $a\neq b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H|>0$, $|C_{c}\setminus V|>0$ the two summands are independent, so generically
${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$. Modulo the inessential constant $J$ the white/red pattern is essentially rank one. This is the $J+W$ derivation repeatedly given by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 2 and in the previous round.

* Rectangular-emblem idealisation. Write $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ for the white canton and $E=pq^{T}$ for a red emblem $E\subset C$ taken as a rectangle, $W=C-E$. Then
$M=aJ+(a-b)(-C+E)=bJ+(a-b)(J-W)$ is $J,C,E$ three rank-one matrices, ${\rm rk}M\le3$, and with $0<E<C$, $a\neq b$ the three rows
$r_{0}=a{\bf1}$, $r_{1}=[b^{w},a^{\,n-w}]$, $r_{2}=[b^{p},a^{k},b^{q},a^{\,n-w}]$
are generically independent. Hence ${\rm rk}M=3$ generically, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, ${\rm rk}P=2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator. This is the $J-C+E$ three-dimensional essential model quoted by Colleagues 2,3,5,7,10, and the “rank 3, 4 counting the constant” statement. Colleagues 7 and 10 in round 2 continue to defend this as the resolution-independent maximal rank under the standard rectangular block idealisation; Colleague 10 explicitly rejects double-counting the constant to reach 4.

* Pixel refinement / continuum limit. On a genuine $m\times n$ raster the emblem boundary is staircased. On the $h$ canton rows the row sections are distinct, so formally ${\rm rk}E\ge h$ and ${\rm rk}M\le h+1\le\min\{m,n\}$. By refining the grid the formal rank can be made arbitrarily large, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, infinite in the continuum limit. This unboundedness is repeatedly noted by Colleagues 1,4,6.

Current tension therefore remains:
– geometric cross: essential rank one for $W$, rank two for the $a,b$-valued matrix $M$, the $J+W$ bound;
– rectangular emblem idealisation: essential rank two for $W$, rank three for $M$, the usual $J-C+E$ bound quoted in the literature;
– formal pixel rank unbounded with resolution.

Round 2 has strengthened the derivation of the rank-one white matrix $(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ for the actual Tongan cross, with a clear consensus among 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 that the resolution-independent geometric rank is 2, i.e. 3 if the constant is counted as an independent factor in the $J-C+E$ idealisation. Colleagues 7 and 10 persist with the rectangular-emblem maximal rank 3 generic value. Unresolved is which interpretation the question intends: the true geometric $J+W$ rank 2, the conventional $J-C+E$ essential rank 3, or the unbounded formal supremum over pixelations.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I continue to align with C7 and C10 on the rectangular idealization: the three observable row signatures (uniform outer red field, canton rows outside either arm of the cross, and canton rows intersected by an arm) already span the full row space once the constant background is absorbed into linear combinations of those blocks. Refinement arguments that produce higher formal rank rely on stair-casing that effectively introduces non-rectangular boundaries, which the standard model excludes. Consequently the maximal attainable rank under the flag’s actual geometry stays exactly three.

5.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and
$0$ on a red pixel. Then with $c=a-b$

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a{\bf 1}_{R}+b{\bf 1}_{W}=bJ+c{\bf 1}_{R}=aJ+(b-a)W,
\qquad {\bf 1}_{R}=J-W ,
\end{equation*}
so modulo the harmless rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.

Let $C_{r}\subset[m]$ , $C_{c}\subset[n]$ be the rows and columns of the
white canton and let $H\subset C_{r}$ , $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows
and columns of the horizontal and vertical arm of the red cross in the
canton. Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

\[
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V}.
\]

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}}$, $u_{H}={\bf1}_{H}$, $v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}}$,
$v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

\[
W_{ij}=\bigl(u_{r}-u_{H}\bigr)_{i}\bigl(v_{c}-v_{V}\bigr)_{j}
      =u_{w,i}v_{w,j},\qquad 
u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H},\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V},
\]

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$,
and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

\[
{\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff|R_{w}|>0,\ |C_{w}|>0,
\]

and

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T})
\]

is the sum of the rank one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two
geometrically distinct rows,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$, and
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2,
\]

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are
linearly independent so that generically

\[
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2,
\]

with ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.
Modulo the inessential constant $bJ$ the red–white pattern is
essentially rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.
This is the resolution independent $J+W$ description of the true
axis-aligned Tongan cross, $P=J-W=J-(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ a
rank-one red emblem, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ-(b-a)C+(b-a)E$ lies in
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, i.e.
essential rank $2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.  That is the
familiar $J-C+E$ three-block count, the $+1$ being the trivial constant
$J$.  Formally on a stair-cased pixelation ${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1$ with
$h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ and the formal supremum over refinements is
$\min\{m,n\}$.  The geometric, resolution independent rank of the
actual flag is the $1+1$ $J+W$ rank two, i.e. essential rank one, quoted
above. ∎

2.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  Then up to the harmless scalar $c=a-b$

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+c{\bf1}_{R}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\bf1}_{R}=J-W ,$$
so modulo the rank one translation $aJ$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of
the white indicator $W$.

Let $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ be the white canton in the upper hoist and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal
arm and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the
canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff

$$i\in C_{r}\setminus H,\qquad j\in C_{c}\setminus V ,$$

i.e. with $u_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =(u_{c}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j} , $$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence with
$u_{w}=u_{c}-u_{H}$, $v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}$

$$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$$

is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ where $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$ and
$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$.  In particular

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0, $$

and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.

Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct row types,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{w}}$ on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2, $$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are linearly
independent.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad{\rm rk}W=1,\qquad{\rm rk}P=2, $$

${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones summand the $0\!-\!1$ white, and hence the red,
pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two-term
description.

In the usual rectangular-emblem idealisation $W_{0}=C-E$ with a single
rank-one red rectangle $E\subset C$, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E$,
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$, one obtains the coarse bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$,
generically ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$, which is the $J-C+E$
three-block model often quoted in the literature.  For the true
Tongan cross the four rank-one terms $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the
single product $(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the
resolution-independent essential rank is the $J+W$ rank two above,
$1$ modulo the trivial constant.

Remark on rasterisation.  On a literal $m\times n$ pixelation the
staircased boundary makes the $h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ canton rows pairwise
different, so formally ${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and
$\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$.  The $2$, i.e. the
$3$ with the constant counted in the rectangular idealisation, is the
resolution independent geometric value. ∎

3.text:
Write $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white.  Put $P=J-W$ for the red indicator.  Then

$$M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W , $$

so up to the harmless rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the white indicator.  Let $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ be the rows and
columns of the canton and let $H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be
the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of
the red cross.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
        {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V} , $$

i.e. with $u_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},
v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$W=(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},
\qquad u_{w}= {\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\;
       v_{w}= {\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V},  $$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence the white set is the Cartesian
product $R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$,
$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$,

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\ |C_{w}|>0, $$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Up to permutation there are only two
geometrically distinct rows

* $r_{0}\equiv a{\bf1}$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{w}}$ on
  $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-W\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2, $$

and for $a\neq b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are
linearly independent.  Up to the inessential all-ones shift the white,
and hence the red, pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$, ${\rm rk}P=1$ essentially, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the
constant kept.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1, $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.
Modulo $J$ this is the familiar $J+W$ two-term, i.e. essential rank
one, description of the Tongan cross.

In particular $P=J-W=J-(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and
$M=aJ-(a-b)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and
$E=(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ the rank-one red part of the canton.
The $J-C+E$ three-term $ {\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, description
is the rectangular-emblem idealisation $W=C-E_{0}$ with a single
rank-one red emblem $E_{0}\subset C$.  For the true axis-aligned Tongan
cross the four rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single
product $(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the resolution independent
essential rank is the $J+W$ rank two, $1$ modulo the constant, quoted
above.  The formal pixel rank can be made $\le\min\{m,n\}$ by
staircasing a curvilinear boundary, the $2$ being the geometric
resolution independent value. ∎

9.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  Up to the harmless translation

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+(a-b){\bf1}_{R}
     =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\bf1}_{R}=J-W ,
\end{equation*}
so mod $J$ the rank is the rank of the white indicator.

Put the white canton in the rows $C_{r}$ and the columns $C_{c}$ and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ be the set of rows occupied by the horizontal arm of
the red cross and $V\subset C_{c}$ the set of columns occupied by the
vertical arm.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

\[
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V},
\]

i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H}$,
$v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

\[
W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},
\qquad 
u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H},\;\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V},
\]

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic
matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V$.  In particular

\[
\operatorname{rk}W=1,
\]

and $W\ne0$ as soon as the canton and the cross are non–trivial.  Up to
the inessential all-ones matrix

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)
\]

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Hence

\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le\operatorname{rk}J+\operatorname{rk}W\le2 .
\]

Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct rows,
$r_{0}\equiv a{\bf1}$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ and
$r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\overline{C_{c}\setminus
V}}$ on $i\in C_{r}\setminus H$, and the same two column types.
For $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H|>0$, $|C_{c}\setminus V|>0$ the two
summands $J$ and $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent and

\[
\operatorname{rk}M=2,\qquad\operatorname{rk}W=1,\qquad
\operatorname{rk}{\bf1}_{R}=2,
\]

and $\operatorname{rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.
Modulo the trivial constant $J$ the white, and hence the red, pattern is
essentially rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$,
the familiar $J+W$ description.  In particular
${\bf1}_{R}=J-(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ is $J$ plus a rank-one
matrix.  This is the resolution independent geometric rank of the real
axis-aligned Tongan cross.

Remark.  In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one canton and $E=pq^{T}$
a rank-one red emblem, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E$ lies in
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ and $\operatorname{rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, i.e.
essential rank two for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.  Formally on an
$m\times n$ raster the staircased boundary gives
$\operatorname{rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and $\sup_{m,n}
\operatorname{rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the continuum limit being infinite
rank.  The $J+u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ two-term model above is the usual
resolution-independent essential rank, $2$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix and
$1$ modulo the constant. ∎

6.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ for the all ones matrix and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff
the $(i,j)$ pixel is white and $0$ otherwise.  Then $P=J-W$ is the red
indicator and

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+(a-b)P_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W_{ij},\qquad
c:=b-a,
\end{equation*}
so that up to the harmless rank one translation $aJ$ the rank of $M$
is the rank of the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator $W$.

Put the canton in the upper hoist and let $C_{r}\subset[m]$ and
$C_{c}\subset[n]$ be the rows and columns of the canton and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm
and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the canton
$W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff

$$i\in C_{r}\setminus H,\qquad j\in C_{c}\setminus V .$$

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},\,v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

\[
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
       {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}
     =(u_{r}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j},
\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton},
\]
i.e. with $u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H},\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}$

\[
W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},\qquad 
u_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\qquad 
v_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V},
\]

the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V$ inside the canton.
Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ and $W\ne0$ for a non-trivial canton and cross.
In particular

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-W)
\]

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only the two geometrically
distinct row types

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on the rows $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}
        \oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$ on the rows $i\in C_{r}\setminus H$,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2,
\]

and for $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H|>0,\;|C_{c}\setminus V|>0$ the two
summands $J$ and $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically

\[
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=1\ {\rm mod}\ J,
\]

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Discarding the
inessential all-ones shift the red–white pattern is essentially rank
one, $W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$, $J+P$
description.  In the conventional $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ rectangular-emblem
notation $W=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ and $E$ a rank-one emblem this
is quoted as ${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3$, generically
$3$, i.e. $2$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix modulo the trivial constant
$J$.  This is the resolution independent essential rank of the genuine
axis-aligned Tongan cross. ∎

8.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and
$0$ on a red pixel, $P=J-W$.  Up to the inessential scalar
$c=a-b$

$$M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+cP=aJ+(b-a)W  ,
\qquad P+W=J, $$

so modulo the rank one matrix $J$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of the
white indicator $W$.  Put the canton $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ in the upper
hoist and let $H\subset C_{r}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm of the
red cross in the canton and $V\subset C_{c}$ the columns of the vertical
arm.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff
its row is outside the horizontal arm and its column is outside the
vertical arm,

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
        {\bf1}_{j\notin V},\qquad i\notin C_{r}\ {\rm or}\ i\in H
        \Longrightarrow W_{i\ast}=0 .
$$

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},
v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad 
u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H},\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}, $$
i.e. on the whole picture $W_{ij}=u_{w,i}v_{w,j}$.  Hence the white set
is the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$,
$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$, and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  In particular

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0, $$

and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank one constant matrix $J$ and the rank one matrix
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two geometrically
distinct rows, 

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$, 
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Hence

$${\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2, $$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are
linearly independent.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2, $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones shift $bJ$ the red–white pattern is essentially
rank one,

$$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad 
P=J-W, $$

i.e. the usual $J+W$ two term description.  This is the resolution
independent essential rank of the genuine axis-aligned Tongan cross,
$1$ modulo the constant and $2$ with the constant kept.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation $W_{0}=C-E$ with
$C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one canton and a single rank-one red emblem
$E\subset C$, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E$ lies in
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically ${\rm rk}M=3$,
${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$.  The $1+1+1$ $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ three block model is
the rectangular block approximation of the cross.  For the true cross
the four rank-one terms $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single product
$(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the essential, resolution
independent, model is the $J+W$ rank two, i.e. essential rank one,
model above.  On a literal $m\times n$ raster the formal pixel rank is
$\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and can be made arbitrarily large with
refinement, the $2$ being the usual geometric essential value, quoted
as $3$ with the constant written out in the $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$
idealisation. ∎

1.text:
Write $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff $(i,j)$ is white and
$0$ otherwise.  Then

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+(a-b){\bf1}_{R}=aJ+(b-a)W,
\qquad {\bf1}_{R}=J-W ,$$

so modulo the $J$--translation the problem is the rank of the white
indicator.  Put the canton in the upper hoist,
$C_{r}\subset[m]$, $C_{c}\subset[n]$, and let $H\subset C_{r}$,
$V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of
the vertical arm of the red cross in the canton.  Off the canton
$W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V} .$$

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},\,v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},
\qquad 
u_{w}= {\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\;v_{w}= {\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V},
$$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with
$R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$ and $W\equiv0$ off
the canton.  Hence ${\rm rk}\,W=1$, $W\not\equiv0$ for a non trivial
canton and cross, and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  In particular

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2 ,
$$

and up to permutation there are essentially two geometrically distinct
rows

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  For $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$
the two summands $J$ and $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent, so
generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad{\rm rk}W=1,\qquad{\rm rk}{\bf1}_{R}=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, for the degenerate case $a=b$.
Removing the inessential all-ones summand $bJ$ the $0\!-\!1$ white,
and hence the red, pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two term description.
In the conventional $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ rectangular-emblem writing
$W_{0}=C-E$, $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E$ a rank-one red
emblem, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}$ is the sum of the three rank-one matrices
$J,C,E$ and the coarse resolution independent bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$
with generic equality ${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. ${\rm rk}M=2$ up to the
trivial constant, is obtained.  This is the $1+1$ essential model;
modulo the constant it is the often quoted essential rank one white
pattern, rank two for the $a,b$-valued matrix itself. ∎

4.text:
Write $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise, $P=J-W$ the red indicator.  Up to the harmless
scalar $c=a-b$,

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+cP=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad 
P=J-W,
\end{equation*}
so modulo the rank one translation $aJ$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of
the white indicator $W$.

Put $C_{r},C_{c}$ for the rows and columns of the white canton and
$H\subset C_{r},V\subset C_{c}$ for the rows of the horizontal arm and
the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the canton
$W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff it lies in
$C_{r}\setminus H$ in the row direction and in $C_{c}\setminus V$ in the
column direction, i.e.

\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V}, \qquad 
W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T} .
\end{equation*}
With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$ and $u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H},\,v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}$,

\begin{equation*}
W_{ij}=u_{w,i}v_{w,j},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
\end{equation*}
$W\equiv0$ off the canton and $W\not\equiv0$ for a non trivial canton
and cross.  The white set is the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus
V$, and $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ is the usual rank–one $0\!-\!1$ pattern.

Hence

\begin{equation*}
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-W)
\end{equation*}
is the sum of the rank one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank one matrix
$W$.  Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct row
types,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on the rows $i\notin C_{r}$ and on the rows $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus
  a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$ on the rows $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2,
\end{equation*}
and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are linearly
independent.  In particular

\[
{\rm rk}M=2\quad a\ne b,\qquad {\rm rk}M=1\iff a=b,
\]

${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the constant $J$ kept and
${\rm rk}P=1$ modulo $J$.
Removing the inessential all-ones shift the red/white pattern is
essentially rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$,
$M=bJ+(a-b)P$, $P=J-W$, the familiar $J+W$ two term description.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation $W_{0}=C-E$ with
$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and a rank one emblem $E\subset C$,

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in{\rm span}\{J,C,E\},
\]

${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, i.e. ${\rm rk}M=2$ up to the trivial
constant $J$.  The four rank one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ of the true
Tongan cross collapse to the single product
$(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{T}$, so the resolution independent
geometric rank of the genuine axis-aligned cross is the $J+W$ rank two,
essential rank one, value above.  The often quoted $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$
three block bound is the rectangular-emblem $W=C-E$ approximation. ∎

public_text.10: I continue to align with C7 and C10 on the rectangular idealization: the three observable row signatures (uniform outer red field, canton rows outside either arm of the cross, and canton rows intersected by an arm) already span the full row space once the constant background is absorbed into linear combinations of those blocks. Any attempt to introduce a fourth independent direction—whether by treating the constant, canton, and emblem as separate outer products or by separating the horizontal and vertical arms—collapses because the white region inside the canton is itself a single Cartesian product after the cross is removed. The J–C–E decomposition therefore remains a sharp upper bound of three, attained generically for a ≠ b. Refinement arguments that produce higher formal rank rely on stair-casing that effectively introduces non-rectangular boundaries, which the standard model excludes. Consequently the maximal attainable rank under the flag’s actual geometry stays exactly three.
public_text.7: The rectangular idealization continues to supply the cleanest resolution-independent model: the matrix is spanned by the constant background J together with the two geometrically distinct blocks C (canton) and the single outer-product term that encodes the white remainder after the cross is removed. Those three rank-one pieces already produce every observed row vector—uniform outer field, canton rows missing the vertical arm, and canton rows intersected by the arm—while the linear dependence among any purported fourth signature follows immediately from the Cartesian-product structure inside the canton. Attempts to exhibit an independent fourth direction require either stair-casing that violates axis-aligned boundaries or an artificial splitting of the collapsed (u_r – u_H)(v_c – v_V)^T term, neither of which is licensed by the flag’s actual geometry. Consequently the generic attainable rank remains exactly 3 for a ≠ b; the constant is absorbed into the three observed row types and does not generate a fourth independent direction.
public_text.5:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and
$0$ on a red pixel. Then with $c=a-b$

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a{\bf 1}_{R}+b{\bf 1}_{W}=bJ+c{\bf 1}_{R}=aJ+(b-a)W,
\qquad {\bf 1}_{R}=J-W ,
\end{equation*}
so modulo the harmless rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.

Let $C_{r}\subset[m]$ , $C_{c}\subset[n]$ be the rows and columns of the
white canton and let $H\subset C_{r}$ , $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows
and columns of the horizontal and vertical arm of the red cross in the
canton. Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

\[
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V}.
\]

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}}$, $u_{H}={\bf1}_{H}$, $v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}}$,
$v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

\[
W_{ij}=\bigl(u_{r}-u_{H}\bigr)_{i}\bigl(v_{c}-v_{V}\bigr)_{j}
      =u_{w,i}v_{w,j},\qquad 
u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H},\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V},
\]

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$,
and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

\[
{\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff|R_{w}|>0,\ |C_{w}|>0,
\]

and

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T})
\]

is the sum of the rank one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two
geometrically distinct rows,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$, and
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2,
\]

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are
linearly independent so that generically

\[
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2,
\]

with ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.
Modulo the inessential constant $bJ$ the red–white pattern is
essentially rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.
This is the resolution independent $J+W$ description of the true
axis-aligned Tongan cross, $P=J-W=J-(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E=u_{e}v_{e}^{T}$ a
rank-one red emblem, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ-(b-a)C+(b-a)E$ lies in
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, i.e.
essential rank $2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.  That is the
familiar $J-C+E$ three-block count, the $+1$ being the trivial constant
$J$.  Formally on a stair-cased pixelation ${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1$ with
$h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ and the formal supremum over refinements is
$\min\{m,n\}$.  The geometric, resolution independent rank of the
actual flag is the $1+1$ $J+W$ rank two, i.e. essential rank one, quoted
above. ∎

Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  Then up to the harmless scalar $c=a-b$

$$M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+c{\bf1}_{R}=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\bf1}_{R}=J-W ,$$

       {\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =(u_{c}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j} , $$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence with

is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product

$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$.  In particular

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0, $$

and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$$

Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct row types,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$,

and the same two column types.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2, $$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are linearly
independent.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad{\rm rk}W=1,\qquad{\rm rk}P=2, $$

${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones summand the $0\!-\!1$ white, and hence the red,
pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two-term

In the usual rectangular-emblem idealisation $W_{0}=C-E$ with a single
rank-one red rectangle $E\subset C$, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E$,
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$, one obtains the coarse bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$,

three-block model often quoted in the literature.  For the true
Tongan cross the four rank-one terms $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the

Write $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white.  Put $P=J-W$ for the red indicator.  Then

$$M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W , $$

so up to the harmless rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the white indicator.  Let $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ be the rows and
columns of the canton and let $H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be
the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of
the red cross.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
        {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V} , $$

i.e. with $u_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},
v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$W=(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},
\qquad u_{w}= {\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\;
       v_{w}= {\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V},  $$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence the white set is the Cartesian
product $R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$,
$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$,

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\ |C_{w}|>0, $$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Up to permutation there are only two
geometrically distinct rows

* $r_{0}\equiv a{\bf1}$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{w}}$ on
  $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-W\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2, $$

and for $a\neq b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are
linearly independent.  Up to the inessential all-ones shift the white,
and hence the red, pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$, ${\rm rk}P=1$ essentially, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the
constant kept.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1, $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.
Modulo $J$ this is the familiar $J+W$ two-term, i.e. essential rank
one, description of the Tongan cross.

In particular $P=J-W=J-(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and
$M=aJ-(a-b)C+(a-b)E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and
$E=(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ the rank-one red part of the canton.
The $J-C+E$ three-term $ {\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, description
is the rectangular-emblem idealisation $W=C-E_{0}$ with a single
rank-one red emblem $E_{0}\subset C$.  For the true axis-aligned Tongan
cross the four rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single
product $(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the resolution independent
essential rank is the $J+W$ rank two, $1$ modulo the constant, quoted
above.  The formal pixel rank can be made $\le\min\{m,n\}$ by
staircasing a curvilinear boundary, the $2$ being the geometric
resolution independent value. ∎

Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  Up to the harmless translation

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a{\bf1}_{R}+b{\bf1}_{W}=bJ+(a-b){\bf1}_{R}
     =aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad {\bf1}_{R}=J-W ,
\end{equation*}
so mod $J$ the rank is the rank of the white indicator.

Put the white canton in the rows $C_{r}$ and the columns $C_{c}$ and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ be the set of rows occupied by the horizontal arm of
the red cross and $V\subset C_{c}$ the set of columns occupied by the
vertical arm.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

\[
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V},
\]

i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H}$,
$v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

\[
W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},
\qquad 
u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H},\;\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V},
\]

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic
matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V$.  In particular

\[
\operatorname{rk}W=1,
\]

and $W\ne0$ as soon as the canton and the cross are non–trivial.  Up to
the inessential all-ones matrix

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)
\]

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Hence

\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le\operatorname{rk}J+\operatorname{rk}W\le2 .
\]

Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct rows,
$r_{0}\equiv a{\bf1}$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ and
$r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\overline{C_{c}\setminus
V}}$ on $i\in C_{r}\setminus H$, and the same two column types.
For $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H|>0$, $|C_{c}\setminus V|>0$ the two
summands $J$ and $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent and

\[
\operatorname{rk}M=2,\qquad\operatorname{rk}W=1,\qquad
\operatorname{rk}{\bf1}_{R}=2,
\]

and $\operatorname{rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.
Modulo the trivial constant $J$ the white, and hence the red, pattern is
essentially rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$,
the familiar $J+W$ description.  In particular
${\bf1}_{R}=J-(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ is $J$ plus a rank-one
matrix.  This is the resolution independent geometric rank of the real
axis-aligned Tongan cross.

Remark.  In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one canton and $E=pq^{T}$
a rank-one red emblem, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E$ lies in
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ and $\operatorname{rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, i.e.
essential rank two for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator.  Formally on an
$m\times n$ raster the staircased boundary gives
$\operatorname{rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and $\sup_{m,n}
\operatorname{rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, the continuum limit being infinite
rank.  The $J+u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ two-term model above is the usual
resolution-independent essential rank, $2$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix and
$1$ modulo the constant. ∎

Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ for the all ones matrix and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff
the $(i,j)$ pixel is white and $0$ otherwise.  Then $P=J-W$ is the red
indicator and

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+(a-b)P_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W_{ij},\qquad
c:=b-a,
\end{equation*}
so that up to the harmless rank one translation $aJ$ the rank of $M$
is the rank of the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator $W$.

Put the canton in the upper hoist and let $C_{r}\subset[m]$ and
$C_{c}\subset[n]$ be the rows and columns of the canton and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm
and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the canton
$W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff

$$i\in C_{r}\setminus H,\qquad j\in C_{c}\setminus V .$$

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},\,v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

\[
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
       {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}
     =(u_{r}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j},
\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton},
\]
i.e. with $u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H},\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}$

\[
W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},\qquad 
u_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\qquad 
v_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V},
\]

the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V$ inside the canton.
Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ and $W\ne0$ for a non-trivial canton and cross.
In particular

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-W)
\]

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only the two geometrically
distinct row types

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on the rows $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}
        \oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$ on the rows $i\in C_{r}\setminus H$,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2,
\]

and for $a\ne b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H|>0,\;|C_{c}\setminus V|>0$ the two
summands $J$ and $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically

\[
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=1\ {\rm mod}\ J,
\]

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Discarding the
inessential all-ones shift the red–white pattern is essentially rank
one, $W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$, $J+P$
description.  In the conventional $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ rectangular-emblem
notation $W=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ and $E$ a rank-one emblem this
is quoted as ${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3$, generically
$3$, i.e. $2$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix modulo the trivial constant
$J$.  This is the resolution independent essential rank of the genuine
axis-aligned Tongan cross. ∎

Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and
$0$ on a red pixel, $P=J-W$.  Up to the inessential scalar
$c=a-b$

$$M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+cP=aJ+(b-a)W  ,
\qquad P+W=J, $$

so modulo the rank one matrix $J$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of the
white indicator $W$.  Put the canton $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ in the upper
hoist and let $H\subset C_{r}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm of the
red cross in the canton and $V\subset C_{c}$ the columns of the vertical
arm.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff
its row is outside the horizontal arm and its column is outside the
vertical arm,

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
        {\bf1}_{j\notin V},\qquad i\notin C_{r}\ {\rm or}\ i\in H
        \Longrightarrow W_{i\ast}=0 .
$$

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},
v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad 
u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H},\;v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}, $$
i.e. on the whole picture $W_{ij}=u_{w,i}v_{w,j}$.  Hence the white set
is the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$,
$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$, and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  In particular

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0, $$

and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank one constant matrix $J$ and the rank one matrix
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two geometrically
distinct rows, 

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$, 
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Hence

$${\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2, $$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands are
linearly independent.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2, $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones shift $bJ$ the red–white pattern is essentially
rank one,

$$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad 
P=J-W, $$

i.e. the usual $J+W$ two term description.  This is the resolution
independent essential rank of the genuine axis-aligned Tongan cross,
$1$ modulo the constant and $2$ with the constant kept.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation $W_{0}=C-E$ with
$C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one canton and a single rank-one red emblem
$E\subset C$, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E$ lies in
${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically ${\rm rk}M=3$,
${\rm rk}W_{0}\le2$.  The $1+1+1$ $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ three block model is
the rectangular block approximation of the cross.  For the true cross
the four rank-one terms $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single product
$(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the essential, resolution
independent, model is the $J+W$ rank two, i.e. essential rank one,
model above.  On a literal $m\times n$ raster the formal pixel rank is
$\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and can be made arbitrarily large with
refinement, the $2$ being the usual geometric essential value, quoted
as $3$ with the constant written out in the $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$
idealisation. ∎

for $a=b$. Modulo the inessential constant $J$ the white/red pattern is
essentially rank one, the familiar $J+W$ two-term description. This is the
position of Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in rounds 0-3 and the derivation
$W=(u_c-u_H)(v_c-v_V)^T$ is now a clear consensus.

* Rectangular-emblem idealisation. Write $C=u_c v_c^T$ for the white canton
and $E=pq^T$ for a red emblem taken as a rectangle, $W_0=C-E$.
Then $M=aJ+(b-a)W_0=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$,
${\rm rk}M\le3$, and with $0<E<C$, $a\ne b$ the three rows
$r_0=a{\bf1}$, $r_1=[b^w,a^{\,n-w}]$, $r_2=[b^p,a^k,b^q,a^{\,n-w}]$ are
generically independent. Hence generic ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W_0\le2$,
${\rm rk}P=2$ for the $0$–$1$ red indicator. This is the $J-C+E$ three-block
model quoted by Colleagues 2,3,5,7,10 and the “rank 3, 4 counting the constant”
statement. Colleagues 7 and 10 in round 3 persist that the three observable
row signatures already span the row space and that the constant is absorbed,
so the maximal attainable rank under the standard rectangular block
idealisation stays exactly three for $a\ne b$.

* Pixel refinement / continuum limit. On a genuine $m\times n$ raster the
boundary is staircased. On the $h=|C_r|$ canton rows the row sections are
distinct, so formally ${\rm rk}E\ge h$ and ${\rm rk}M\le h+1\le\min\{m,n\}$.
By refining the grid the formal rank can be made arbitrarily large,
$\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$, infinite in the continuum limit.
This unboundedness is repeatedly noted by Colleagues 1,4,6.

Current tension: geometric cross gives resolution-independent essential rank
one for $W$, rank two for the $a,b$-valued $M$; rectangular emblem idealisation
gives essential rank two for $W$, rank three for $M$; formal pixel rank is
unbounded. Round 3 strengthened the $W=(u_r-u_H)(v_c-v_V)^T$ derivation and
the $J+W$ rank-two consensus among the majority, while Colleagues 7 and 10
continue to defend the conventional $J-C+E$ maximal rank three.
Unresolved is which reading the question intends: true geometric $J+W$
rank 2, conventional $J-C+E$ rank 3, or the unbounded formal supremum over
pixelations. Earlier notes about double-counting the constant, the collapse
$C,H,V,H\cap V\to (u_c-u_H)(v_c-v_V)^T$, and the $h+1$ row bound remain
relevant.
reflection_text.9:
The matrix is $M=aJ+(b-a)W=bJ+(a-b)P$ with $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$ and $W$ the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator. Modulo the inessential $J$ the rank is that of $W$.

For the true axis-aligned Tongan cross let $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ be the white canton and $H\subset C_{r}$, $V\subset C_{c}$ the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm. Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =(u_{c}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j}=u_{w,i}v_{w,j}$,

i.e. $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ is the characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$(C_{r}\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_{c}\!\setminus\!V)$. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$, $W\neq0$ for a non-trivial canton and cross, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T})$

is $J$ plus a rank-one matrix. Up to permutation there are essentially two geometrically distinct rows,

${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2$,

${\rm rk}M=2$ for generic $a\neq b$, $|C_{r}\setminus H|>0$, $|C_{c}\setminus V|>0$, and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$. Modulo $J$ the white, and hence the red, pattern is essentially rank one, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the constant kept, essential rank $1$. This is the $J+W$ two-term resolution-independent geometric description endorsed in round 3 by C1,C2,C3,C4,C5,C6,C8,C9.

The $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ three-block idealisation $W_{0}=C-E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and $E=pq^{T}\subset C$ a single rank-one red emblem gives $M=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$, ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically ${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. essential rank $2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ pattern. This is the rectangular-emblem model quoted as rank $3$, $4$ counting the constant, and the source of the rank-$3$ claims of C10 and C7 in round 3.
