I keep rank $2$ generic, $1$ degenerate, as the correct geometric value, with rank $3$ noted as the usual rectangular-emblem idealisation and unbounded formal pixel rank under refinement.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The rectangular idealization supplies the cleanest resolution-independent model: the matrix is spanned by the constant background J together with the two geometrically distinct blocks C (canton) and the single outer-product term that encodes the white remainder after the cross is removed. Those three rank-one pieces already produce every observed row vector—uniform outer field, canton rows missing the vertical arm, and canton rows intersected by the arm—while the linear dependence among any purported fourth signature follows immediately from the Cartesian-product structure inside the canton. Attempts to exhibit an independent fourth direction require either stair-casing that violates axis-aligned boundaries or an artificial splitting of the collapsed (u_r – u_H)(v_c – v_V)^T term, neither of which is licensed by the flag’s actual geometry. Consequently the generic attainable rank remains exactly 3 for a ≠ b; the constant is absorbed into the three observed row types and does not generate a fourth independent direction. This matches the J–C–E decomposition bound that several colleagues have already noted as sharp once the cross arms are recognized as collapsing into one product rather than two separate outer products.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The J–C–E rectangular-emblem model continues to supply the cleanest resolution-independent upper bound. With the constant background J, the single outer-product canton C, and the single outer-product remainder E after the cross is excised, we obtain three linearly independent rank-one terms whose span already reproduces every observable row signature: the uniform outer field, the canton rows lying entirely outside both arms, and the canton rows intersected by an arm. Because the white remainder inside the canton is itself a Cartesian product, any purported fourth direction generated by separating the horizontal and vertical arms collapses algebraically into the single product (u_r – u_H)(v_c – v_V)^T; thus the three-block count is sharp and is attained generically whenever a ≠ b. The repeated claims that the same three terms further collapse to only two independent directions overlook that the constant J cannot be expressed as a linear combination of C and E once the arms have removed a positive-measure sub-rectangle from the canton; the resulting row vectors remain affinely independent. Consequently the generic attainable rank is exactly three, and any higher formal rank arises only from stair-casing that violates the axis-aligned geometry of the flag itself.

3.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white,
$P=J-W$ the red indicator.  Then

$$M=aP+bW=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W , $$

so up to the inessential rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the white indicator $W$.

Put the canton in the rows $C_{r}\subset[m]$ and the columns
$C_{c}\subset[n]$ and let $H\subset C_{r}$, $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows
of the horizontal arm and the columns of the vertical arm of the red
cross in the canton. Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =(u_{c}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j},$$

with $u_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$.  Put $u_{w}=u_{c}-u_{H}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H}$ and
$v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$.  Then on the whole
picture

$$W_{ij}=u_{w,i}v_{w,j},\qquad 
W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},$$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  The white set is the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$,
so that ${\rm rk}\,W=1$ and $W\not\equiv0$ for a non-trivial canton and
cross.  Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank one matrix
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.

Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct rows,
$r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ and
$r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{w}}$ on $i\in R_{w}$, and the
same two column types.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2,$$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad{\rm rk}W=1,\qquad{\rm rk}P=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Modulo the
inessential constant $bJ$ the red-white pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$, i.e. the usual $J+W$ description.  In particular
$P=J-W=J-(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ is $J$ plus a rank one matrix.

Remark.  In the coarse rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=C-E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank one canton and $E$ a rank
one red emblem, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$,
${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, i.e. ${\rm rk}M=2$ up to the trivial
constant $J$.  This is the $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ three-block count often quoted
in the literature.  For the true axis-aligned Tongan cross the four
rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single product
$(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, so the resolution independent geometric
rank is the $J+W$ rank two quoted above, $1$ modulo $J$.  On a literal
$m\times n$ rasterisation the formal rank can be made $\le h_{c}+1$ with
$h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ and is unbounded under refinement. ∎

2.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel, $0$ on a red
pixel.  Put $P=J-W$.  Then

$$
M=aP+bW=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W,
$$

so modulo the harmless rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Let $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ be the
rows and columns of the white canton in the upper hoist and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal
arm and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the
canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff

$$
i\in C_{r}\setminus H,\qquad j\in C_{c}\setminus V ,
$$

i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},
v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}
       {\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =(u_{r}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j},
$$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Put
$u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H}$,
$v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$.  Then on the whole
picture

$$
W=u_{w}v_{w}^{\!T},
\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
$$

$W\ne0\iff |C_{r}\setminus H|>0,\ |C_{c}\setminus V|>0$, and the white
set is the Cartesian product $R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with
$R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$, the four corner
rectangles of the canton.  Hence

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{\!T}
  =bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{\!T}\bigr)
$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$u_{w}v_{w}^{\!T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two geometrically
distinct row types,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus
  a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$ on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically

$$
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2,
$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1\iff a=b$, $M=aJ$.  Modulo the inessential all-ones
shift $bJ$ the red–white pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$ 
two-term description, essential rank $1$ and $2$ with the constant kept.

In particular $P=J-W=J-(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$.  The
conventional $J-C-E$ rectangular-emblem writing $W_{0}=C-E$ with
$C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and a single rank-one red emblem $E\subset
C$ gives $M=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ and the coarse
resolution independent bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, i.e. $2$
up to the trivial constant.  That three-block bound is the $W_{0}=C-E$
rectangular idealisation.  For the genuine axis-aligned Tongan cross
the four rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single product
$(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the resolution independent
geometric rank is the $J+W$ rank two quoted above, $1$ modulo $J$.
Formally on an $m\times n$ raster the stair-cased boundary gives
${\rm rk}M\le |C_{r}|+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and the formal supremum over
refinements is $\min\{m,n\}$.  The $2$, $3$ in the $J-C-E$
idealisation, is the usual essential geometric value. ∎

1.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and
$0$ on a red pixel, $P=J-W$.  Then

$$M=aP+bW=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W $$

so mod the rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the rank of the
$0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Up to a permutation of rows and columns the
flag is the union of a red field and a white canton $C_{r}\times C_{c}$
in the upper hoist with the red cross $H\times C_{c}\cup C_{r}\times V$
in the canton, $H\subset C_{r}$, $V\subset C_{c}$.  Off the canton
$W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff its row is outside the
horizontal arm and its column is outside the vertical arm,

$$
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V},\qquad i\notin C_{r}\Longrightarrow W_{i*} \equiv0 ,
$$

i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$
W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},\qquad
u_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\;v_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V},
$$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic
matrix of the Cartesian product $R_{w}\times C_{w}$,
$R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$, and

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0,$$

on the whole picture.  In particular

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}
   =bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)
$$

is the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two
geometrically distinct rows,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two distinct column types.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically therefore

$$
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones shift $bJ$ the red–white pattern is essentially
rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, i.e. the
familiar $J+W$ two term, $J+P$, description of the genuine axis-aligned
Tongan cross.  Modulo the trivial constant this is the often quoted
essential rank one white, hence red, pattern.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem writing $W_{0}=C-E$,
$C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one canton and $E$ a rank-one red emblem,
$M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$,
one obtains the coarse resolution-independent bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$,
generically ${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. ${\rm rk}M=2$ up to the trivial constant
$J$.  The $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ three block count is the $1+1+1$ rectangular
idealisation of the cross; for the true axis-aligned cross the four
rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single product
$(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the geometric, resolution
independent value is the $J+W$ rank two above, essential rank one
modulo $J$.  On a literal $m\times n$ raster the formal rank can be made
$\le h_{c}+1$ with $h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=
\min\{m,n\}$, the continuum limit being unbounded; the $2$, quoted as
$3$ with the constant written out, is the usual geometric value. ∎

8.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  Then $P=J-W$ is the red indicator and
up to $c=a-b$

$$M=aP+bW=bJ+cP=aJ+(b-a)W ,$$

so modulo the harmless rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the white indicator.

Put the canton in $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ and let $H\subset C_{r}$,
$V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of
the vertical arm of the red cross in the canton.  Off the canton
$W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff its row is outside
$H$ and its column is outside $V$,

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =(u_{r}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j},\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;C},$$

with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$.  Put
$u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\;
v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$.  Then on the whole
picture

$$W_{ij}=u_{w,i}v_{w,j},\qquad W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},$$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$,
$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$ and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

$${\rm rk}W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0,$$

and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}
  =bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr) $$

is the sum of the rank one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank one matrix
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two geometrically
distinct rows,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{w}}$ on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2, $$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2, $$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones shift $bJ$ the red–white pattern is essentially
rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$, $P=J-W$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two term
description.  This is the resolution independent geometric rank of the
genuine axis aligned Tongan cross, $1$ modulo the constant and $2$ with
the constant kept.

Remark.  In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=C-E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one canton and a single
rank-one red emblem $E\subset C$, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E$
lies in ${\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$,
i.e. essential rank $2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ indicator.  The four rank-one
pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ of the true cross collapse to the single product
$(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ above, giving the $J+W$ rank two,
essential rank one, model.  On a literal $m\times n$ raster formal
staircasing gives ${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and unbounded
supremum under refinement, the $2$ being the usual geometric
resolution-independent value, quoted as $3$ in the $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$
rectangular block count. ∎

9.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white.
Put $P=J-W$ for the red indicator.  Then

$$M=aP+bW=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W ,$$

so up to the harmless rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator $W$.

Put the white canton in the rows $C_{r}$ and the columns $C_{c}$ and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ be the set of rows of the horizontal arm of the red
cross in the canton and $V\subset C_{c}$ the set of columns of the
vertical arm.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is
white iff its row is outside $H$ and its column is outside $V$,

$$W_{ij}={\bf 1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf 1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf 1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf 1}_{j\notin V}\qquad i\notin C_{r}\;{\rm or}\;i\in H
       \Longrightarrow W_{i*}=0 .
$$

With $u_{r}={\bf 1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf 1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf 1}_{C_{c}},
v_{V}={\bf 1}_{V}$,

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},\qquad
u_{w}={\bf 1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\;v_{w}={\bf 1}_{C_{c}\setminus V},
$$

i.e. up to the zero off the canton $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic
matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$,
$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$.  Hence

${\rm rk}W=1$ and $W\ne0$ for a non trivial canton and cross, and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.
Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct rows,
$r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ and
$r_{1}=b{\bf 1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf 1}_{\bar C_{w}}$ on
$i\in R_{w}$, and the same two column types.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2,$$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2,$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Modulo the
inessential all-ones shift the red–white pattern is essentially rank
one,

$$W=(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad
P=J-W,$$

the familiar $J+W$, i.e. $J+P$, two-term description of the genuine
axis-aligned Tongan cross.  In particular ${\rm rk}P=1$ mod $J$ and
${\rm rk}M=1$ mod $J$.

Remarks.  In the usual rectangular-emblem idealisation $W_{0}=C-E$ with
$C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and a single rank-one red emblem
$E\subset C$, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$
gives the coarse bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, i.e. essential
rank $2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ pattern.  This is the $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ three
block count often quoted.  The four rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ of
the true cross collapse to the single product
$(u_{c}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the resolution independent
geometric rank of the actual flag is the $J+W$ rank two quoted above,
essential rank one modulo $J$.  Formal stair-casing can make the
formal pixel rank $\le h_{c}+1$, with supremum $\min\{m,n\}$,
the $2$ being the usual geometric essential value. ∎

4.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and let $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise, $P=J-W$. Then

$$M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W ,$$

so mod the harmless rank one translation $aJ$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator.  Put the white canton in the
rows $C_{r}$ and the columns $C_{c}$ and let $H\subset C_{r}$, 
$V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of
the vertical arm of the red cross.  Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the
canton a pixel is white iff its row is outside the horizontal arm and
its column is outside the vertical arm,

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
        {\bf1}_{j\notin V},\qquad i\notin C_{r}\Longrightarrow W_{i*}=0 .
$$

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},\qquad 
u_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\;v_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V},
$$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$,
and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  In particular ${\rm rk}W=1$, $W\ne0$ for
a non-trivial canton and cross, and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two
geometrically distinct rows,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$ 
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Hence

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2, $$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically therefore

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2, $$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones shift $bJ$, the $0\!-\!1$ white, and hence the
red, pattern is essentially rank one,

$$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T},\qquad 
P=J-W, $$

i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two-term description.  Modulo the trivial
constant this is the resolution independent essential rank one of the
real axis-aligned Tongan cross, rank two for the $a,b$-valued matrix
itself.  In the coarse rectangular-emblem writing $W_{0}=C-E$,
$C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$, $E$ a rank one red emblem, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}\in
{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ gives the often quoted coarse bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$,
generically $3$, i.e. $2$ up to the trivial constant $J$. ∎

5.text:
Write $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$ and put $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  $P=J-W$ is the red indicator and

\begin{equation*}
M=aP+bW=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W ,
\end{equation*}
so up to the harmless rank one translation $J$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the white indicator $W$.

Put the white canton in the rows $C_{r}$ and the columns $C_{c}$ and
let $H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal
arm and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross in the canton.
Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff

\[
W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V},\qquad i\notin C_{r}\Longrightarrow W_{i*}=0,
\]

i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},
v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

\[
W_{ij}=(u_{r}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j},
\qquad
W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},
\quad
u_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\;
v_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V},
\]

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  The white set is the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$,
so on the whole picture $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of a
single outer product.  In particular

\[
{\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\ |C_{w}|>0,
\]

and

\[
M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)
\]

is the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.
Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct row types

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Hence

\[
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le 1+1=2,
\]

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically

\[
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2,
\]

and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones shift $bJ$ the $0\!-\!1$ white, and hence the red,
pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two-term
description.

In particular $P=J-W=J-(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and
$M=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E$ with $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and
$E=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ the rank-one red part of the canton.
Modulo the trivial constant this is the $1+1$ essential model,
$1$ for $W$ and $2$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix.  Written in the usual
$J-C+E$ rectangular-emblem notation $W_{0}=C-E$ this is often quoted as
${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}E\le3$, generically $3$,
i.e. $2$ for the $a,b$-valued matrix and $1$ modulo the constant.
The $3$ is the $J-C+E$ block count; the resolution independent geometric
value is the $J+u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ rank two, essential rank one, model
above. ∎

6.text:
Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is white
and $0$ otherwise, $P=J-W$.  Then

$$M_{ij}=aP_{ij}+bW_{ij}=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W ,\qquad P+W=J,
$$

so up to the harmless rank one translation $aJ$ the rank of $M$ is the
rank of the $0\!-\!1$ white indicator $W$.  Put the canton in the upper
hoist, $C_{r}\subset[m]$, $C_{c}\subset[n]$, and let
$H\subset C_{r}$ and $V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm
and the columns of the vertical arm of the red cross in the canton.
Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff

$$i\in C_{r}\setminus H,\qquad j\in C_{c}\setminus V ,$$

i.e. with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},\,u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},\,v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
\,v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V}
     =\bigl(u_{r}-u_{H}\bigr)_{i}\bigl(v_{c}-v_{V}\bigr)_{j},
\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;the\;canton},$$

and with $u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H}$,
$v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$

$$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T} $$

is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$.
In particular

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\ |C_{w}|>0, $$

and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

$$M=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$$

is the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank-one matrix
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two geometrically
distinct row types,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2 ,$$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2, $$

${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$, $M=aJ$, and modulo the inessential all-ones
shift $bJ$ the red–white pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two-term
description.  In particular $P=J-W=J-(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ is
$J$ plus a rank-one matrix, ${\rm rk}P=1$ mod $J$, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the
constant kept.

This is the resolution independent geometric rank of the genuine
axis-aligned Tongan cross.  In the usual coarse $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$
rectangular-emblem writing $W_{0}=C-E$, $C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the canton and
$E$ a rank-one red emblem, $M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in
{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$ gives the quoted coarse bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$,
generically ${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. ${\rm rk}M=2$ up to the trivial constant
$J$, which is the $1+1+1$ block model often quoted in the literature.
The four rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ of the true cross collapse to
the single product $(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, so the essential
resolution independent model is the $J+W$ rank two, rank one modulo $J$,
model above. ∎

public_text.10: The rectangular idealization supplies the cleanest resolution-independent model: the matrix is spanned by the constant background J together with the two geometrically distinct blocks C (canton) and the single outer-product term that encodes the white remainder after the cross is removed. Those three rank-one pieces already produce every observed row vector—uniform outer field, canton rows missing the vertical arm, and canton rows intersected by the arm—while the linear dependence among any purported fourth signature follows immediately from the Cartesian-product structure inside the canton. Attempts to exhibit an independent fourth direction require either stair-casing that violates axis-aligned boundaries or an artificial splitting of the collapsed (u_r – u_H)(v_c – v_V)^T term, neither of which is licensed by the flag’s actual geometry. Consequently the generic attainable rank remains exactly 3 for a ≠ b; the constant is absorbed into the three observed row types and does not generate a fourth independent direction. This matches the J–C–E decomposition bound that several colleagues have already noted as sharp once the cross arms are recognized as collapsing into one product rather than two separate outer products.
public_text.7: The J–C–E rectangular-emblem model continues to supply the cleanest resolution-independent upper bound. With the constant background J, the single outer-product canton C, and the single outer-product remainder E after the cross is excised, we obtain three linearly independent rank-one terms whose span already reproduces every observable row signature: the uniform outer field, the canton rows lying entirely outside both arms, and the canton rows intersected by an arm. Because the white remainder inside the canton is itself a Cartesian product, any purported fourth direction generated by separating the horizontal and vertical arms collapses algebraically into the single product (u_r – u_H)(v_c – v_V)^T; thus the three-block count is sharp and is attained generically whenever a ≠ b. The repeated claims that the same three terms further collapse to only two independent directions overlook that the constant J cannot be expressed as a linear combination of C and E once the arms have removed a positive-measure sub-rectangle from the canton; the resulting row vectors remain affinely independent. Consequently the generic attainable rank is exactly three, and any higher formal rank arises only from stair-casing that violates the axis-aligned geometry of the flag itself.

Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the pixel $(i,j)$ is white,

$$M=aP+bW=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W , $$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Modulo the
inessential constant $bJ$ the red-white pattern is essentially rank one,
$W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$, i.e. the usual $J+W$ description.  In particular

Remark.  In the coarse rectangular-emblem idealisation
$W_{0}=C-E$ with $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank one canton and $E$ a rank

in the literature.  For the true axis-aligned Tongan cross the four
rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single product

rank is the $J+W$ rank two quoted above, $1$ modulo $J$.  On a literal

matrix of the Cartesian product $R_{w}\times C_{w}$,
$R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$, and

$${\rm rk}\,W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0,$$

on the whole picture.  In particular

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}
   =bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)
$$

is the sum of the rank-one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank-one white
matrix $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$.  Up to permutation there are only two
geometrically distinct rows,

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ and on $i\in H$,
* $r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$
  on $i\in R_{w}$,

and the same two distinct column types.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le1+1=2,
$$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the two summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically therefore

$$
{\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2,
$$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones shift $bJ$ the red–white pattern is essentially
rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$, i.e. the
familiar $J+W$ two term, $J+P$, description of the genuine axis-aligned
Tongan cross.  Modulo the trivial constant this is the often quoted
essential rank one white, hence red, pattern.

In the conventional rectangular-emblem writing $W_{0}=C-E$,
$C=u_{r}v_{c}^{T}$ the rank-one canton and $E$ a rank-one red emblem,
$M=aJ+(b-a)W_{0}=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$,
one obtains the coarse resolution-independent bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$,
generically ${\rm rk}M=3$, i.e. ${\rm rk}M=2$ up to the trivial constant
$J$.  The $J\!-\!C\!-\!E$ three block count is the $1+1+1$ rectangular
idealisation of the cross; for the true axis-aligned cross the four
rank-one pieces $C,H,V,H\cap V$ collapse to the single product
$(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}$ and the geometric, resolution
independent value is the $J+W$ rank two above, essential rank one
modulo $J$.  On a literal $m\times n$ raster the formal rank can be made
$\le h_{c}+1$ with $h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=
\min\{m,n\}$, the continuum limit being unbounded; the $2$, quoted as
$3$ with the constant written out, is the usual geometric value. ∎

Write $J={\bf 1}_{m\times n}$ and $W_{ij}=1$ iff the $(i,j)$ pixel is
white and $0$ otherwise.  Then $P=J-W$ is the red indicator and
up to $c=a-b$

$$M=aP+bW=bJ+cP=aJ+(b-a)W ,$$

rank of the white indicator.

Put the canton in $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ and let $H\subset C_{r}$,
$V\subset C_{c}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm and the columns of
the vertical arm of the red cross in the canton.  Off the canton
$W\equiv0$ and on the canton a pixel is white iff its row is outside
$H$ and its column is outside $V$,

$$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}
       {\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =(u_{r}-u_{H})_{i}(v_{c}-v_{V})_{j},\qquad W\equiv0\;{\rm off\;C},$$

with $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},
v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$.  Put
$u_{w}=u_{r}-u_{H}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},\;
v_{w}=v_{c}-v_{V}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$.  Then on the whole

$$W_{ij}=u_{w,i}v_{w,j},\qquad W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T},$$

i.e. $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$,
$C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$ and $W\equiv0$ off the canton.  Hence

$${\rm rk}W=1,\qquad W\ne0\iff |R_{w}|>0,\;|C_{w}|>0,$$

and

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}
  =bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr) $$

is the sum of the rank one all-ones matrix $J$ and the rank one matrix

* $r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$,

and the same two column types.  Consequently

$${\rm rk}M\le{\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2, $$

and for $a\ne b$, $|R_{w}|>0$, $|C_{w}|>0$ the summands $J$ and
$u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are linearly independent.  Generically

$${\rm rk}M=2,\qquad {\rm rk}W=1,\qquad {\rm rk}P=2, $$

with ${\rm rk}M=1$, $M=aJ$, in the degenerate case $a=b$.  Removing the
inessential all-ones shift $bJ$ the red–white pattern is essentially
rank one, $W=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$, $P=J-W$, i.e. the familiar $J+W$ two term
description.  This is the resolution independent geometric rank of the
genuine axis aligned Tongan cross, $1$ modulo the constant and $2$ with
the constant kept.

Remark.  In the conventional rectangular-emblem idealisation

reflection_text.5:
The deliberation remains three-way.

* True geometric axis-aligned cross.  
With $C_r,C_c$ the canton rows/cols and $H\subset C_r$, $V\subset C_c$ the
horizontal/vertical arms, off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton
$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_r}{\bf1}_{j\in C_c}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}$.
Hence $W=(u_r-u_H)(v_c-v_V)^T=u_wv_w^T$ with $u_w={\bf1}_{C_r\setminus H}$,
$v_w={\bf1}_{C_c\setminus V}$. The white set is the Cartesian product
$R_w\times C_w$, $R_w=C_r\setminus H$, $C_w=C_c\setminus V$, so
${\rm rk}W=1$, $W\neq0$ for a non-trivial cross. 
$M=aJ+(b-a)W=bJ+(a-b)(J-W)$ is $J$ plus rank one. Up to permutation there
are only two geometrically distinct row types $r_0\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_r$
or $i\in H$ and $r_1=b{\bf1}_{C_w}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_c}$
on $i\in R_w$, same for columns. Hence ${\rm rk}M\le2$, and for $a\neq b$,
$|R_w|>0$, $|C_w|>0$, ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}P=2$, degenerating
to $1$ for $a=b$. Modulo the inessential all-ones shift the pattern is
essentially rank one, the familiar $J+W$ two-term, $J+P$, description.
This is the position of Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in rounds 0-4 and is now a
clear consensus.

* Rectangular-emblem idealisation.  
Write $C=u_r v_c^T$ for the white canton and $E=pq^T$ for a red emblem
taken as a rectangle, $W_0=C-E$. Then $M=aJ+(b-a)W_0=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)E\in
{\rm span}\{J,C,E\}$, ${\rm rk}M\le3$. With $0<E<C$, $a\neq b$ the three
row signatures $r_0=a{\bf1}$, $r_1=[b^w,a^{n-w}]$, $r_2=[b^p,a^k,b^q,a^{n-w}]$
are generically independent, so generic ${\rm rk}M=3$, ${\rm rk}W_0\le2$,
${\rm rk}P=2$ for the $0\!-\!1$ red indicator. This is the $J-C+E$ three-block
model quoted by Colleagues 2,3,5,7,10 and the “rank 3, 4 counting the
constant” statement. Colleagues 7 and 10 in round 4 persist that the three
observable row signatures already span the row space and that the constant
is absorbed, so the maximal attainable rank under the standard rectangular
block idealisation stays exactly three for $a\neq b$.

* Pixel refinement / continuum limit.  
On a genuine $m\times n$ raster the boundary is staircased. On the
$h=|C_r|$ canton rows the row sections are distinct, so formally
${\rm rk}E\ge h$ and ${\rm rk}M\le h+1\le\min\{m,n\}$. By refining the grid
the formal rank can be made arbitrarily large, $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}
=\min\{m,n\}$, infinite in the continuum limit. This unboundedness is
repeatedly noted by Colleagues 1,4,6.

Current tension: geometric cross gives resolution-independent essential
rank one for $W$, rank two for the $a,b$-valued $M$; rectangular emblem
idealisation gives essential rank two for $W$, rank three for $M$; formal
pixel rank is unbounded. Round 4 strengthened the $W=(u_r-u_H)(v_c-v_V)^T$
derivation and the $J+W$ rank-two consensus among the majority, while
Colleagues 7 and 10 continue to defend the conventional $J-C+E$ maximal
rank three. Unresolved is which reading the question intends: true
geometric $J+W$ rank 2, conventional $J-C+E$ rank 3, or the unbounded
formal supremum over pixelations. Earlier notes about double-counting the
constant, the collapse $C,H,V,H\cap V\to(u_r-u_H)(v_c-v_V)^T$, and the
$h+1$ row bound remain relevant.

The flag is a red field with a white canton $C_{r}\times C_{c}$ in the hoist and a red cross inside the canton. Let $H\subset C_{r}$ be the rows of the horizontal arm and $V\subset C_{c}$ the columns of the vertical arm. Off the canton $W\equiv0$ and on the canton

$W_{ij}= {\bf1}_{i\in C_{r}}{\bf1}_{j\in C_{c}}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}$.

With $u_{r}={\bf1}_{C_{r}},u_{H}={\bf1}_{H},v_{c}={\bf1}_{C_{c}},v_{V}={\bf1}_{V}$,

$W=(u_{r}-u_{H})(v_{c}-v_{V})^{T}=u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$,
$u_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{r}\setminus H},v_{w}={\bf1}_{C_{c}\setminus V}$,
so $W$ is the $0\!-\!1$ characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product
$R_{w}\times C_{w}$ with $R_{w}=C_{r}\setminus H$, $C_{w}=C_{c}\setminus V$, and $W\equiv0$ off the canton. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ if the cross is non-trivial, $W\neq0$ iff $|R_{w}|>0,|C_{w}|>0$.

With $J={\bf1}_{m\times n}$ and $M=aP+bW$, $P=J-W$,

$M=bJ+(a-b)P=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u_{w}v_{w}^{T}=bJ+(a-b)\bigl(J-u_{w}v_{w}^{T}\bigr)$

is $J$ plus a rank-one matrix. Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct row types:
$r_{0}\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_{r}$ or $i\in H$ and
$r_{1}=b{\bf1}_{C_{w}}\oplus a{\bf1}_{V}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_{c}}$ on $i\in R_{w}$,
and the same two column types. Thus

${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W\le2$,

and for $a\neq b$, $|R_{w}|>0,|C_{w}|>0$ the summands $J$ and $u_{w}v_{w}^{T}$ are independent, so generically ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}P=2$ with the constant kept, ${\rm rk}P=1$ mod $J$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$. Formal pixel rank is resolution dependent. On an $m\times n$ raster the stair-cased boundary makes the $h_{c}=|C_{r}|$ canton rows pairwise distinct, so formally ${\rm rk}M\le h_{c}+1\le\min\{m,n\}$ and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=\min\{m,n\}$; the continuum limit is unbounded. The resolution-independent geometric value is the $J+W$ rank $2$, i.e. essential rank $1$ for the $0\!-\!1$ pattern, commonly quoted as rank $3$ for the $J,C,E$ rectangular idealisation with the constant counted.

$W_{ij}={\bf1}_{i\in C_r}{\bf1}_{j\in C_c}{\bf1}_{i\notin H}{\bf1}_{j\notin V}
      =(u_r-u_H)_i(v_c-v_V)_j$,

so with $u_w={\bf1}_{C_r\setminus H}$, $v_w={\bf1}_{C_c\setminus V}$

$W=u_wv_w^T$

is the characteristic matrix of the Cartesian product $(C_r\!\setminus\!H)\times(C_c\!\setminus\!V$. Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$, $W\equiv0$ off the canton, and

$M=aJ+(b-a)u_wv_w^T=bJ+(a-b)(J-u_wv_w^T)$

is $J$ plus a rank-one matrix. Up to permutation there are only two geometrically distinct row types, $r_0\equiv a$ on $i\notin C_r$ or $i\in H$ and $r_1=b{\bf1}_{C_w}\oplus a{\bf1}_{\bar C_w}$ on $i\in C_r\setminus H$, and the same two column types. Thus
